definition_zh: 功能的；实用的；起作用的；函数式的
definition_en: relating to how something works or operates; designed to be practical rather than decorative
core_image: 一把没有花纹、但每处弯折都贴合手掌的椅子

pos.zh: 功能的；实用的；函数式的；（医学）功能性的

senses.title: Relating to function
senses.definition: concerned with how something works rather than with how it looks
senses.definitionCN: 关注某物如何运作、而非外观的
senses.example: The report gives a functional description of the engine, not a drawing.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告给出的是发动机的功能描述，而不是图纸。
senses.why: functio means 'performance'. Functional marks the question 'what does it do?', leaving appearance and origin aside.
senses.whyCN: functio 意为“执行”。functional 标记的是“它做什么”这个问题，把外观与来源放在一边。

senses.title: Practical and working
senses.definition: designed to be useful and to work well, without decoration
senses.definitionCN: 设计上追求好用、能运作，不加装饰的
senses.example: The kitchen is small but highly functional.
senses.exampleCN: 这间厨房很小，但非常实用。
senses.why: Modern design made functional a virtue. A functional object is judged by whether it performs its job, not by ornament.
senses.whyCN: 现代设计把 functional 变成一种美德。评判一件 functional 的物品，看它是否履行职责，而不是看装饰。

senses.title: Functional design
senses.titleCN: 功能主义的：形式跟着用途走
senses.definition: in architecture and design, following the principle that form should serve use
senses.definitionCN: 建筑与设计中遵循“形式服从用途”原则的
senses.example: The building's functional style leaves the concrete and glass bare.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋建筑的功能主义风格让混凝土与玻璃保持素面。
senses.why: This sense names a movement, not just a quality. Functionalism turned 'what it does' into a rule for 'how it should look'.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项命名的是一场运动，而不只是性质。功能主义把“它做什么”变成“它该长什么样”的规则。

senses.title: Organized by role
senses.titleCN: 按职能划分的：谁管什么
senses.definition: describing an organization divided by the work each part performs rather than by product or region
senses.definitionCN: 指按各部分承担的工作而非产品或地区划分的组织结构
senses.example: The company moved from a regional to a functional structure.
senses.exampleCN: 公司从地区型结构转为职能型结构。
senses.why: In management the function is a department's job. A functional structure groups people by what they do, not by where they sit.
senses.whyCN: 管理中的 function 是部门的职责。职能型结构按“做什么”分组，而不是按“在哪里”分组。

senses.title: Mathematics and programming
senses.titleCN: 函数式的：把计算当函数
senses.definition: in mathematics and computing, relating to functions or to a style of programming based on them
senses.definitionCN: 数学与计算中与函数有关，或指以函数为基础的编程风格
senses.example: Functional programming treats computation as the evaluation of functions.
senses.exampleCN: 函数式编程把计算视为对函数的求值。
senses.why: The mathematical function is a fixed mapping from input to output. Functional programming builds everything from such mappings.
senses.whyCN: 数学函数是从输入到输出的固定映射。函数式编程用这类映射构建一切。

senses.title: Medical: no visible damage
senses.titleCN: 功能性的：查不出器质病变
senses.definition: in medicine, describing a disorder in which the organ works badly without structural damage
senses.definitionCN: 医学上指器官运作不良但没有结构损害的疾病
senses.example: She was diagnosed with a functional bowel disorder.
senses.exampleCN: 她被诊断为功能性肠病。
senses.why: Here functional marks the absence of structural cause. The complaint is real, but the tests show a working organ behaving badly.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 functional 标记“没有结构病因”。症状真实，但检查显示器官结构正常、运作失常。

senses.title: Operational and usable
senses.definition: in a state of working order, ready to be used
senses.definitionCN: 处于可运作状态、随时可使用的
senses.example: The website is functional again after the server move.
senses.exampleCN: 服务器迁移之后，网站又能正常使用了。
senses.why: This is the condition sense: not how it is designed, but whether it currently runs. A functional machine is one that answers when switched on.
senses.whyCN: 这是状态义：不是问如何设计，而是问现在是否运转。functional 的机器就是打开开关会响应的机器。

senses.title: Grammar that follows use
senses.titleCN: 功能语法的：按用途解释形式
senses.definition: in linguistics, describing an approach that explains forms by the jobs they perform in communication
senses.definitionCN: 语言学中指按形式在交流中承担的作用来解释形式的取向
senses.example: Functional grammar asks why a passive is chosen, not just how it is formed.
senses.exampleCN: 功能语法问的是为什么选被动式，而不只是它如何构成。
senses.why: Linguistics uses the word for explanations based on use. A form exists because it does a job, which is the functional argument in one line.
senses.whyCN: 语言学用这个词指基于用途的解释。形式存在是因为它承担一项任务，这就是功能论证的一句话版本。

intro.en: Functional is function plus -al. Function comes from Latin functio 'performance', from fungi 'to perform'. The root is fung-, unrelated to fundus 'bottom'; the word concerns doing, not founding.
intro.cn: functional 是 function 加 -al。function 来自拉丁 functio“执行”，源头是 fungi“履行”。词根是 fung-，与 fundus“底部”无关；这个词讲“做”，不讲“奠基”。

items.en: fungi 'to perform, discharge' is the source. Its past participle functus produces function, defunct and functionary; the root has no connection with fundus.
items.cn: fungi“履行、执行”是源头。其过去分词 functus 生出 function、defunct、functionary；这个词根与 fundus 没有联系。

items.en: functio named the discharge of a duty or role. English function keeps both the everyday 'purpose' sense and the mathematical 'mapping' sense.
items.cn: functio 命名职责或角色的履行。英语 function 同时保留日常“用途”义与数学“映射”义。

items.en: Function enters English in the 16th century. The mathematical sense develops later, once algebra needs a word for a relation between quantities.
items.cn: function 于 16 世纪进入英语。数学义较晚发展，是代数需要一个词来表示量之间关系的结果。

items.en: Functional adds -al, from Latin -alis, to function. The adjective first means 'relating to a function', then 'practical' in design language.
items.cn: functional 在 function 后加 -al（来自拉丁 -alis）。这个形容词先指“与功能有关”，后来在设计语言中转为“实用的”。

items.en: In the 20th century functional becomes a slogan of architecture and design, where form is supposed to follow use.
items.cn: 20 世纪 functional 成为建筑与设计的口号，主张形式服从用途。

items.en: Functional programming names a computing style, while functional disorder names illness without structural damage. Both keep the same root idea of performance.
items.cn: 函数式编程命名一种计算风格，而功能性疾病命名无结构损害的疾病。两者都保留“执行”的词根观念。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the funct- stem but splits by suffix and prefix; the near-meaning group all describe something judged by use rather than appearance.
note.cn: 形近组共享 funct- 词干，但按后缀与前缀分流；近义组都描述“按用途而非外观评判”的东西。

entries.definition: a purpose, role or mathematical relation. It is the thing; functional describes it.
entries.definitionCN: 用途、职责或数学关系。它是名词；functional 描述它。

entries.definition: the set of functions or the working state. It is a noun; functional is the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 功能集合或运作状态。它是名词；functional 是形容词。

entries.definition: no longer existing or working. de- 'away' plus functus 'performed' gives 'having finished performing'.
entries.definitionCN: 已废止的；不再运作的。de-“离开”加 functus“已履行”，意为“已停止履行”。

entries.definition: useful and sensible in real conditions. It is wider than functional and often about judgment.
entries.definitionCN: 在真实条件下有用且合理。它比 functional 宽泛，常涉及判断。

entries.definition: in working order and ready for use. It stresses readiness, while functional can also describe design.
entries.definitionCN: 处于运作状态、可供使用。它强调就绪，而 functional 也可描述设计。

entries.definition: designed for usefulness, often at the cost of beauty. It is more judgmental than functional.
entries.definitionCN: 为实用而设计，常牺牲美观。它比 functional 更具评价色彩。

entries.definition: good enough to use, though not elegant. It is close to functional but implies adequacy rather than design intent.
entries.definitionCN: 够用、可服役的，虽不精美。它接近 functional，但暗示“够用”而非设计意图。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: fungi 'perform' gives function and functional: the word always asks what a thing performs.
normal.cn: fungi“履行”生出 function 与 functional：这个词始终在问一件东西履行什么。

normal.en: functional design, functional requirement and functional programming are the three strongest collocations.
normal.cn: functional design、functional requirement、functional programming 是三个最强的搭配。

normal.en: functional disorder means the organ looks fine but works badly, which shows the word is about performance.
normal.cn: functional disorder 指器官外观正常却运作不良，说明这个词讲的是“执行”。

normal.en: Do not confuse functional with foundational: fung- is perform, fund- is bottom.
normal.cn: 别把 functional 与 foundational 混淆：fung- 是执行，fund- 是底部。

normal.en: A functional object is not necessarily beautiful, and a beautiful object is not necessarily functional.
normal.cn: functional 的物品不一定美，美的物品不一定 functional。

abstract.en: Think of a chair with no ornament whose every angle fits the body.
abstract.cn: 想象一把没有装饰、每个角度都贴合身体的椅子。

abstract.en: Think of a machine that starts on the first try, with no light and no sound wasted.
abstract.cn: 想象一台一次就启动的机器，不浪费一点灯光与声音。

abstract.en: Think of a toolbox where each tool sits in the slot shaped for it.
abstract.cn: 想象工具箱里每件工具都放在为它开好的槽里。

examples.en: The prototype is functional but too heavy to carry.
examples.cn: 样机可以正常使用，但太重，带不动。

examples.en: Functional requirements describe what the system must do.
examples.cn: 功能需求描述系统必须做什么。

examples.en: The patient had functional symptoms but normal scans.
examples.cn: 患者有功能性症状，但扫描正常。

root: 拉丁 fungi“履行、执行” → functio“执行” → 英语 function + -al；词根为 fung-，与 fund-（底部）无关。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one standard: judge it by what it performs, not by what it looks like or where it came from.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享一个标准：按它履行什么来评判，而不是按外观或来源。

core.cn: 核心意象：一把没有装饰、贴合身体的椅子。

branches.en: PERFORMANCE: describing a function, being practical and being in working order are three views of the same 'it works'.
branches.cn: 执行：描述功能、实用、处于可运作状态，是同一个“它能工作”的三种视角。

branches.en: DESIGN: functionalism turns performance into a rule for appearance.
branches.cn: 设计：功能主义把“性能”变成外观规则。

branches.en: ORGANIZATION: a functional structure groups people by the job they perform.
branches.cn: 组织：职能型结构按人们履行的职责分组。

branches.en: ABSTRACT SYSTEMS: mathematics, programming and grammar all explain forms by the mappings or jobs they perform.
branches.cn: 抽象系统：数学、编程与语法都用“执行的映射或任务”来解释形式。

branches.en: MEDICINE: functional marks real symptoms without structural damage, the same 'performance' focus.
branches.cn: 医学：functional 标记真实症状而无结构损害，仍是同一种“执行”焦点。

intro.en: Functional is function plus -al. The funct- stem means 'perform', -ion makes an action noun and -al makes the relational adjective.
intro.cn: functional 是 function 加 -al。funct- 词干意为“履行”，-ion 构成动作名词，-al 构成关系形容词。

latinIntro.en: The family runs from fungi 'perform' through functio 'performance' to English function. Relatives include functional, malfunction, defunct and functionary.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词族从 fungi“履行”经 functio“执行”到英语 function。同族词包括 functional、malfunction、defunct、functionary。

definition_zh: 强迫；限制；约束；束缚
definition_en: to force someone to do something, or to limit and restrict what someone or something can do
core_image: 一根绷紧的绳子把箱子牢牢捆在柱子上，绳子越勒越紧
scene: 货车上，两根绷紧的绑带把木箱死死压住，司机说： The straps constrain the load so it cannot shift.
sceneCN: 这里指第 1 个义项。这里 constrain 是「物理束缚、限制移动」（第 2、3、5 个义项：把东西限制在范围内、用外力捆住）；句意：绑带把货物固定住，使其无法移动。图中可辨识物件：货车、木箱、尼龙绑带、司机。

derivatives.zh: 受限制的；拘谨的；不自然的

senses.title: Force someone to act
senses.definition: to compel a person to do something, whether by authority, necessity or pressure
senses.definitionCN: 以权威、必要性或压力迫使一个人做某事
senses.example: Illness constrained him to give up the trip.
senses.exampleCN: 疾病迫使他放弃了这次旅行。
senses.why: Latin constringere meant 'to bind tightly, fetter'. A bound person has no choice of movement, so the verb naturally covers 'force to act' as well as 'prevent from acting'.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 constringere 意为“紧紧捆住、上镣铐”。被捆住的人没有行动自由，所以这个动词既覆盖“迫使行动”，也覆盖“阻止行动”。

senses.title: Limit what can happen
senses.titleCN: 限制：给可能性画一条边界
senses.definition: to limit the size, amount, range or speed of something
senses.definitionCN: 限制某物的大小、数量、范围或速度
senses.example: A small budget constrained the design from the start.
senses.exampleCN: 预算有限，从一开始就限制了设计。
senses.why: The rope image turns abstract: a budget, a rule or a deadline can act as a rope around a project, holding it inside a boundary.
senses.whyCN: 绳子的意象变得抽象：预算、规则或截止日期都能成为项目周围的绳子，把它圈在边界之内。

senses.title: Hold physically: tied or bound
senses.titleCN: 物理束缚：被绑住、被固定
senses.definition: to hold a body or object physically, so that it cannot move freely
senses.definitionCN: 在物理上固定住身体或物体，使其无法自由移动
senses.example: The patient's arms were constrained by soft straps.
senses.exampleCN: 病人的双臂被软带固定住。
senses.why: This is the original bodily sense of constringere: stringere means 'draw tight', and the strap is drawn tight around the body.
senses.whyCN: 这是 constringere 最初的肉体义：stringere 意为“拉紧”，绑带被拉紧缠在身上。

senses.title: Restrict freedom of action
senses.titleCN: 制约：条件压住行动空间
senses.definition: of conditions, rules or circumstances, to make action narrower or harder
senses.definitionCN: （条件、规则或环境）压缩行动空间，使行动更窄或更难
senses.example: He felt constrained by what his family expected of him.
senses.exampleCN: 他感到被家人的期望所束缚。
senses.why: Social expectations work exactly like a rope: nothing visible touches you, yet the range of possible moves is narrowed.
senses.whyCN: 社会期望的作用就像绳子：看不见任何东西碰到你，可移动的范围却被缩小了。

senses.title: Tighten or narrow a space
senses.titleCN: 收紧：把空间或通道勒窄
senses.definition: to make a passage, opening or movement narrower or tighter
senses.definitionCN: 使通道、开口或运动变得更窄、更紧
senses.example: The narrow doorway constrained the flow of people.
senses.exampleCN: 狭窄的门洞限制了人流的通行。
senses.why: When a tight band presses inward, the space inside shrinks. Constrict is the direct Latin doublet used for this physical squeezing.
senses.whyCN: 当紧箍向内压时，内部空间就变小。constrict 是同一拉丁词直接借入的双式词，专门用于这种物理挤压。

senses.title: Constrained: forced and unnatural
senses.definition: the adjective describes behaviour, style or a smile that looks forced rather than free
senses.definitionCN: 形容词指行为、文风或笑容显得勉强、不自然，而非自在
senses.example: She gave a constrained smile and said nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 她勉强笑了笑，什么也没说。
senses.why: A person who is held in by invisible ropes moves carefully. The participle keeps that physical picture: the movement is correct but not free.
senses.whyCN: 被无形绳索束住的人动作会小心翼翼。分词保留了这幅画面：动作正确，却不自由。

senses.title: Constraint: the rope itself
senses.definition: the noun for a rule, limit or condition that keeps something within bounds
senses.definitionCN: 指把某物限制在范围内的规则、限度或条件
senses.example: Time and money are the main constraints on the project.
senses.exampleCN: 时间和金钱是这个项目的主要限制条件。
senses.why: The -t noun turns the act of binding into the thing that binds. A constraint is the rope, not the pulling.
senses.whyCN: -t 名词把“捆”这个动作变成“捆的东西”。constraint 是那根绳子，而不是拉绳的动作。

senses.title: Constrain a variable in science
senses.titleCN: 科学中的约束：给变量加限定
senses.definition: in mathematics, engineering and statistics, to restrict a variable or parameter to a set of allowed values
senses.definitionCN: 在数学、工程与统计中，把变量或参数限制在允许的取值范围内
senses.example: The model constrains the temperature to stay above zero.
senses.exampleCN: 该模型把温度约束在零度以上。
senses.why: A mathematical constraint is a boundary drawn around possible values, the same boundary a rope draws around a body.
senses.whyCN: 数学上的约束就是画在可能取值周围的边界，与绳子在身体周围画出的边界完全相同。

senses.title: Constrain a feeling or a sound
senses.titleCN: 抑制：把情绪或声音压回去
senses.definition: to hold back an emotion, a reaction or a sound so that it does not show
senses.definitionCN: 压住情绪、反应或声音，使其不外露
senses.example: He constrained his anger until the meeting ended.
senses.exampleCN: 他压住怒火，直到会议结束。
senses.why: A feeling that is held in is literally kept inside the body by tension, which is why constrain can mean suppress rather than merely limit.
senses.whyCN: 被“收住”的情绪 literally 靠身体的紧张被关在里面，所以 constrain 可以表示“压抑”，而不只是“限制”。

intro.en: Constrain came through Old French from Latin constringere 'to bind together, tie tightly, fetter'. Its root stringere 'draw tight' also gives strict, strain, restrict and constrict, so the whole family is about tightening.
intro.cn: constrain 经古法语来自拉丁语 constringere“捆在一起、紧紧绑住、上镣铐”。其词根 stringere“拉紧”还给出 strict、strain、restrict、constrict，整个词族都围绕“收紧”。

items.en: Constringere meant 'to bind together, tie tightly, fetter, shackle, chain', from com- 'together' + stringere 'to draw tight, compress'.
items.cn: constringere 意为“捆在一起、紧紧绑住、上镣铐、加锁链”，由 com-“一起”加 stringere“拉紧、压缩”构成。

items.en: Stringere is reconstructed to PIE *streig- 'to stroke, rub, press'. The reconstruction is standard but unattested, so the deepest step is a scholarly reconstruction rather than a recorded word.
items.cn: stringere 被重构为原始印欧语 *streig-“抚摸、摩擦、压”。该重构是通行的，但没有书面记录，因此最深一步是学术重构而非有记载的词。

items.en: English recorded constreyen in the early 14th century, from the stem of Old French constreindre, meaning both 'urge to action' and 'restrain from it'.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪早期记录 constreyen，来自古法语 constreindre 的词干，同时表示“催促行动”和“阻止行动”两个方向。

items.en: The 'restrain, confine' branch grew stronger, and by the 16th century constrain was the ordinary verb for limiting movement or behaviour.
items.cn: “抑制、限制”这一支逐渐增强，到 16 世纪，constrain 已成为表示限制移动或行为的常用动词。

items.en: Constringe (c. 1600) and constrict (1732, a back-formation from constriction) are the learned doublets of the same Latin word, used mainly for physical squeezing.
items.cn: constringe（约 1600 年）与 constrict（1732 年，由 constriction 逆构）是同一个拉丁词的学术双式词，主要用于物理挤压。

items.en: Modern English splits the work: constrain for abstract limits and forced behaviour, constrict for tubes and passages, and constraint for the limit itself.
items.cn: 现代英语分工明确：constrain 用于抽象限制与被迫行为，constrict 用于管道与通道，constraint 指限制本身。

note.en: The look-alike group contains a different-root neighbour and two same-root doublets; the near-meaning group separates force from limit.
note.cn: 形近组包含一个异根近邻和两个同根双式词；近义组把“强迫”与“限制”分开。

entries.definition: to build or put together. Its root is struere 'pile up', not stringere 'draw tight', so it builds rather than binds.
entries.definitionCN: 建造；组装。它的词根是 struere“堆起”，不是 stringere“拉紧”，所以它是“搭起来”而不是“捆起来”。

entries.definition: to make narrower by squeezing. It is the direct Latin borrowing of the same word that became constrain through French.
entries.definitionCN: 挤压使变窄。它是同一个拉丁词直接借入英语的形式，而 constrain 是经法语传来的。

entries.definition: to interpret words or actions in a particular way. It comes from construere 'build', so it means 'build a meaning'.
entries.definitionCN: 以特定方式解释词语或行为。它来自 construere“建造”，意思是“搭出一种意义”。

entries.definition: to force someone to do something. It is stronger and more formal than constrain and focuses on the pressure to act.
entries.definitionCN: 强迫某人做某事。它比 constrain 更强、更正式，聚焦于“促使人行动”的压力。

entries.definition: to stop someone or something from acting. Re- 'back' marks the direction: holding back, whereas constrain presses from outside.
entries.definitionCN: 阻止某人或某物行动。re-“向后”标出方向：往回拉住，而 constrain 是从外部压住。

entries.definition: to keep something within fixed limits. It is the everyday word for rules and access, and less forceful than constrain.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物保持在固定限度内。它是规则与权限方面的日常用词，力度弱于 constrain。

entries.definition: to keep someone or something inside a space or a set of limits. It stresses the boundary rather than the pulling tight.
entries.definitionCN: 把某人或某物关在某个空间或限度内。它强调边界，而不是“拉紧”。

normalIntro.en: Real pieces only: stringere 'draw tight', the same-root family strict, strain, restrict, constrict, and the noun constraint.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实构件：stringere“拉紧”，同根词族 strict、strain、restrict、constrict，以及名词 constraint。

normal.en: Stringere means 'draw tight'. Constrain is to draw a tight band around someone's choices.
normal.cn: stringere 意为“拉紧”。constrain 就是在人的选择周围拉上一道紧箍。

normal.en: Strict, strain, restrict, constrict, district and stringent all belong to this tightening family; each narrows something in its own way.
normal.cn: strict、strain、restrict、constrict、district、stringent 都属于这个“收紧”词族，各自以自己的方式把某物收窄。

normal.en: Constrain and restrain pull in opposite directions: constrain presses you toward or inside a limit, restrain holds you back from acting.
normal.cn: constrain 与 restrain 的用力方向相反：constrain 把你压向或压进某个限度，restrain 则把你往回拉住、不让行动。

normal.en: A constraint is the rope itself; a constrained smile is the result of the rope being there.
normal.cn: constraint 是绳子本身；constrained smile 是绳子存在造成的结果。

normal.en: In science a constraint is a boundary on allowed values, which is exactly a rope drawn around a set of numbers.
normal.cn: 科学中的 constraint 是允许取值上的边界，字面上就是在一组数字周围拉起的绳子。

abstract.en: Picture a box tied to a post with one tight strap. Nothing is hurt, but every possible movement is now a smaller set.
abstract.cn: 想象一个箱子被一根紧带捆在柱子上。什么都没受伤，但所有可能的移动都变成了一个更小的集合。

abstract.en: The strap can be physical (a seatbelt), social (expectations), financial (a budget) or mathematical (a parameter range).
abstract.cn: 这根带子可以是物理的（安全带）、社会的（期望）、财务的（预算）或数学的（参数范围）。

abstract.en: Because the word names both the pressure and the boundary, English can constrain a person, a project, a variable or a smile with one verb.
abstract.cn: 因为这个词同时命名压力和边界，英语可以用一个动词 constrain 人、项目、变量或笑容。

examples.en: Lack of funding constrained the scope of the study.
examples.cn: 资金不足限制了这项研究的范围。

examples.en: She felt constrained by the rules of the old laboratory.
examples.cn: 她感到被旧实验室的规矩束缚。

examples.en: The valve constrains the flow of water into the tank.
examples.cn: 阀门控制进入水箱的水流。

dict_mnemonic.text: “肯·斯专”——肯（定）用斯（绳）专（门）把箱子捆紧在柱子上 → constrain 束缚、限制

root: 源自拉丁语 constringere“捆紧、上镣铐”，由 com-“一起”+ stringere“拉紧”构成，核心是“用外力把范围勒紧”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of constrain, all built on one tight strap. It can press a person to act, fence a project in, bind a body, squeeze a passage, or hold a feeling inside; the strap changes material, not shape.
sensesIntro.cn: constrain 的九个义项都建立在一根绷紧的带子上。它可以逼人行动、把项目圈住、捆住身体、勒窄通道，或把情绪压在里面；变化的只是带子的材质，形状始终一样。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one strap drawn tight around a box, making every movement smaller.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根带子紧紧勒住箱子，使每一种移动都变小。

branches.en: PRESSURE ON PEOPLE: authority, illness or expectations push a person toward one action or away from others.
branches.cn: 对人的压力：权威、疾病或期望把人推向某个行动，或推离其他行动。

branches.en: BOUNDARIES ON POSSIBILITY: budgets, rules and parameter ranges draw a line around what can happen.
branches.cn: 可能性的边界：预算、规则与参数范围在“能发生什么”周围画出界线。

branches.en: PHYSICAL BINDING: straps, narrow doorways and constricted tubes show the strap literally.
branches.cn: 物理束缚：绑带、狭窄门洞与收缩的管道把“带子”直接呈现出来。

branches.en: WHAT THE STRAP DOES TO THE SELF: behaviour becomes stiff and a feeling is held inside.
branches.cn: 带子对自我的作用：行为变得拘谨，情绪被收在里面。

branches.en: THE STRAP AS OBJECT: constraint is the limit itself rather than the act of limiting.
branches.cn: 作为物体的带子：constraint 指限制本身，而不是施加限制的动作。

intro.en: Constrain has an unusually clear Latin skeleton: con- + string- + -ain (French verb ending). Its English derivatives add -t, -ed, un- and the learned doublets constrict and constringe.
intro.cn: constrain 的拉丁骨架异常清晰：con- + string- + -ain（法语动词词尾）。英语派生词加 -t、-ed、un-，以及学术双式词 constrict、constringe。

latinIntro.en: The Latin stringere family is broad and real: strictus 'drawn tight', constringere, restringere, districtus, and stringens 'binding'. English took some directly and some through French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 stringere 词族庞大而真实：strictus“拉紧的”、constringere、restringere、districtus、stringens“束紧的”。英语有的直接借入，有的经法语借入。

items.example: Rules constrain how the money is spent.
items.exampleCN: 规则限制了这笔钱的使用方式。

items.meaningCN: 限制；约束（-t 构成名词）
items.example: Space is the main constraint on the design.
items.exampleCN: 空间是这项设计的主要限制。

items.meaningCN: 受限制的；拘谨的（-ed 构成分词与形容词）
items.exampleCN: 他的声音听起来很拘谨。

items.meaningCN: 起限制作用的（-ing 构成现在分词）
items.example: The rules are constraining but fair.
items.exampleCN: 这些规则虽有约束，但公平。

items.meaningCN: 不受约束的；自由的（un- 表否定）
items.exampleCN: 她毫无拘束地开心大笑。

items.meaningCN: 压缩；使变窄（同根直接借入）
items.exampleCN: 冷空气使管道收缩。

items.meaning: a narrow or squeezed place; the act of squeezing
items.meaningCN: 压缩；狭窄处（-ion 构成名词）
items.example: A constriction in the artery blocked the flow.
items.exampleCN: 动脉中的一处狭窄阻断了血流。
肌肉使导管收缩。

items.meaningCN: 严格的（同一词根的形容词）
items.example: The school has strict rules about lateness.
items.exampleCN: 这所学校对迟到有严格规定。

items.meaningCN: 限制；限定（同根，re- 表向后）
items.exampleCN: 仅限员工进入。

latinEntries.meaning: to bind together, tie tightly, fetter
latinEntries.meaningCN: 捆在一起；紧紧绑住；上镣铐

latinEntries.meaning: to draw tight, compress, touch lightly

definition_zh: 灵长类动物；灵长目成员；（宗教）首席主教
definition_en: a mammal of the order Primates, or a senior bishop in some churches
core_image: 一只向前看的眼睛、一只能对握的手，再加一条能缠住树枝的尾巴
scene: 动物园的说明牌上画着一只对握的手和一双朝前的眼睛，参观者伸手比了比。 A primate is defined less by its thumb than by the eyes it aims at the next branch.
sceneCN: 这里「灵长类动物」指灵长目的一个成员（第 1 个义项：动物学上的目成员）；句意为灵长类与其说由拇指界定，不如说由那双瞄准下一根树枝的眼睛界定。

pos.zh: 灵长类动物；灵长目成员（可数，复数 primates）
首席主教；教省主教（部分教会用语，读音常作 /ˈpraɪmət/）

derivatives.zh: 拉丁 primas「居首者」→ 灵长目（林奈所定的目名，取「首位」之意）
primate + -logy（希腊「学问」）→ 灵长类学
primacy + -al（关系形容词后缀）→ 首席主教的；首席的（语义偏移：指教会职权）
primus「第一」+ -acy（状态名词后缀）→ 首位；首要地位
primus + -al → 最初的；原始的（语义偏移：从「第一」到「最早」）
primarius「第一等的」→ 初级读本；底漆（语义偏移：起先导作用之物）

senses.title: A member of the order Primates
senses.titleCN: 灵长目成员：动物学上的一个目
senses.definition: a mammal belonging to the order Primates, with grasping hands and forward-facing eyes
senses.definitionCN: 具有抓握的手与朝前双眼的灵长目哺乳动物
senses.example: A primate is defined less by its thumb than by the eyes it aims at the next branch.
senses.exampleCN: 灵长类与其说由拇指界定，不如说由那双瞄准下一根树枝的眼睛界定。
senses.why: Latin primas meant 'of first rank'; Linnaeus gave the order that name, and the word has named its members ever since, with grasping and vision as the usual diagnostic traits.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 primas 意为「居首的」；林奈给这个目取了这个名字，此后这个词便指其成员，抓握与视觉是常用辨识特征。

senses.title: An animal used in research
senses.titleCN: 实验动物：被用于研究的灵长类个体
senses.definition: an individual primate kept or studied in a laboratory setting
senses.definitionCN: 在实验室环境中被饲养或研究的灵长类个体
senses.example: The primate in the cognition study had been trained on touchscreens for years.
senses.exampleCN: 这项认知研究里的灵长类个体已在触摸屏上训练多年。
senses.why: Because primates are close relatives, they became the standard animal for questions about cognition and disease; the noun then names a research subject as much as a taxon.
senses.whyCN: 由于灵长类与人类亲缘近，它们成了认知与疾病问题的标准实验动物；于是这个名词既指分类单元，也指研究对象。

senses.title: A species in an ecosystem
senses.titleCN: 生态中的物种：作为群落一员
senses.definition: a primate species considered as part of an ecological community
senses.definitionCN: 被当作生态群落一员的灵长类物种
senses.example: Every primate in the canopy disperses seeds for the trees that feed it.
senses.exampleCN: 树冠层里的每一种灵长类都在为供养它的树木传播种子。
senses.why: Ecology counts species rather than specimens, so the word shifts to the population level: a primate here means one node in a food web.
senses.whyCN: 生态学数的是物种而非标本，因此这个词转到种群层面：此处的 primate 指食物网中的一个节点。

senses.title: A relative in plain speech
senses.titleCN: 通俗说法：我们的灵长类近亲
senses.definition: an informal way of calling monkeys and apes our close relatives
senses.definitionCN: 把猴与猿称作我们近亲的口语说法
senses.example: The film kept saying that every primate shares most of our genes.
senses.exampleCN: 影片反复说每一种灵长类都与我们共享大部分基因。
senses.why: Plain speech uses the taxonomic word for kinship rather than classification; the tone is warm, and the precision is deliberately loose.
senses.whyCN: 口语用这个分类词谈亲缘而非分类；语气亲切，精确度则有意放宽。

senses.title: A senior bishop
senses.titleCN: 首席主教：某些教会中的教省主教
senses.definition: a bishop holding the highest office in a province or national church
senses.definitionCN: 在教省或全国教会中居最高职位的 bishop
senses.example: The primate of the province presided at the consecration.
senses.exampleCN: 该教省的首席主教主持了祝圣礼。
senses.why: This sense is older in English than the zoological one: Latin primas named a church officer of the first rank, and the ecclesiastical word entered English through French.
senses.whyCN: 这一义在英语中比动物学义更早：拉丁 primas 指居首的教会职务，教会用语经法语进入英语。

senses.title: An attributive label
senses.titleCN: 定语用法：用于研究领域或器官
senses.definition: used before a noun to mark the field or the organ, as in primate cognition
senses.definitionCN: 置于名词前、标记研究领域或器官，如灵长类认知
senses.example: Primate brains are studied for the same reason their hands are.
senses.exampleCN: 研究灵长类的脑，与研究它们的手出于同一理由。
senses.why: Taxonomic nouns regularly become modifiers in English; the attributive use says which order the study or organ belongs to, without naming an individual.
senses.whyCN: 分类名词在英语中经常作修饰语；定语用法说明研究或器官属于哪个目，而不指名个体。

senses.title: The order as a category
senses.titleCN: 作为分类范畴：目这一级
senses.definition: the order itself as a taxonomic category
senses.definitionCN: 分类学上「目」这一级本身
senses.example: Primates is the order; primate is the member, and the two are not interchangeable.
senses.exampleCN: Primates 是目，primate 是成员，两者不可互换。
senses.why: A category and its members share a stem but not a grammatical number: one is a capitalized plural taxon, the other a countable noun.
senses.whyCN: 范畴与其成员共享词干，但数不同：一个是首字母大写的复数分类名，一个是可数名词。

senses.title: Popular use for monkeys and apes
senses.titleCN: 通俗泛指：猴与猿的统称
senses.definition: in everyday use, any monkey or ape, with no taxonomic care
senses.definitionCN: 日常使用中泛指任何猴或猿，不计分类
senses.example: The sign said primates, and the children looked for the monkeys first.
senses.exampleCN: 牌子上写着灵长类，孩子们先去找猴子。
senses.why: Popular usage keeps the word but drops the boundaries; the result is a broad everyday sense that a specialist would not use in writing.
senses.whyCN: 通俗用法保留词形却不管边界；结果是一个专家不会在写作中使用的宽泛日常义。

senses.title: A grade in evolution
senses.titleCN: 演化等级：以灵长类水平描述适应
senses.definition: a level of adaptation described as primate-grade, rather than a formal taxon
senses.definitionCN: 以「灵长类水平」描述的适应等级，而非正式分类单元
senses.example: Some early mammals are described as primate-like without being placed in the order.
senses.exampleCN: 有些早期哺乳动物被描述为「似灵长类」，却没有被归入该目。
senses.why: Grade thinking lets writers use a taxon's name for a body plan that appeared before the taxon did, which is why primate-like exists beside primate.
senses.whyCN: 等级思维让作者用一个分类名来指在该分类出现之前就有的身体方案，这就是 primate-like 与 primate 并存的原因。

intro.en: Primate has two histories that meet in one spelling: a church office of the first rank, and an order of mammals named by Linnaeus. Both go back to the Latin word for 'first'.
intro.cn: primate 的两段历史汇于一种拼写：居首的教会职务，以及林奈命名的哺乳动物目。两者都回到拉丁语的「第一」。

items.en: Primus 'first' is a fully attested Latin ordinal with a clear Indo-European background; unlike many words in this batch, its Latin form is not in doubt.
items.cn: primus「第一」是书证充分的拉丁序数词，印欧背景清楚；与本批许多词不同，其拉丁形式并无争议。

items.en: Primas, primatis meant 'one of the first rank, chief'; it was used of leading men and later of leading bishops.
items.cn: primas, primatis 意为「居首者、首领」；先用于显要人物，后用于首席主教。

items.en: English primate entered through Old French primat in the medieval period, meaning a bishop of the highest rank in a province.
items.cn: 英语 primate 于中世纪经古法语 primat 进入，指教省中职位最高的主教。

items.en: Linnaeus placed humans and apes in one order and called it Primates, 'the first ones'; he did not publish a detailed reason, so the motive behind the name is inferred rather than documented.
items.cn: 林奈把人与猿放进同一个目，取名 Primates，意为「居首者」；他没有发表详细理由，因此命名动机是推断而非有据。

items.en: The order later expanded to include lemurs and other groups, while the church sense continued separately in ecclesiastical English.
items.cn: 这个目后来扩展到包含狐猴等类群，而教会义在教会英语中另行延续。

items.en: Source uncertain (naming motive): Linnaeus's reason for choosing Primates is not established, and explanations offered for it are interpretations; the date 1758 is that of the tenth edition.
items.cn: 来源不确定（命名动机）：林奈选用 Primates 的理由没有定论，各种解释均属推测；1758 年指《自然系统》第十版之年。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same 'first' stem, which are the commonest look-alike errors; group two holds the wider and narrower animal categories.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「第一」词干、最常被看错的词；第二组是更宽与更窄的动物类别。

entries.definition: The state of being first in rank; it shares the stem but names a position, not an animal.
entries.definitionCN: 居首的状态；共享词干，但指位置，不指动物。

entries.definition: Belonging to the earliest stage; the sense moved from 'first in rank' to 'first in time'.
entries.definitionCN: 属于最早阶段的；词义从「位次第一」转到「时间最早」。

entries.definition: From primarius 'of the first class': an introductory book or a first coat of paint.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 primarius「第一等的」：入门书或第一道漆。

entries.definition: The capitalized plural is the order's name; the singular is one member of it.
entries.definitionCN: 首字母大写的复数是目名；单数指其中一个成员。

entries.definition: Any warm-blooded vertebrate that feeds its young; primates are one order within it.
entries.definitionCN: 任何哺乳幼崽的恒温脊椎动物；灵长目只是其中一个目。

entries.definition: The tailless large primates, gorillas, chimpanzees, orangutans and humans; narrower than primate.
entries.definitionCN: 无尾的大型灵长类，即大猩猩、黑猩猩、猩猩与人；比 primate 窄。

entries.definition: Most non-ape primates, usually with tails; the everyday word children reach for first.
entries.definitionCN: 多数非猿的灵长类，通常有尾；孩子最先想到的日常词。

entries.definition: A member of the family containing great apes and humans, one branch of the primates.
entries.definitionCN: 含大猿与人类的那个科的成员，是灵长类中的一支。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin layers, real ranks and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁层次、真实层级与真实搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Primas 'of the first rank' gives both the church officer and Linnaeus's order of 'the first ones'.
normal.cn: primas「居首的」既给出教会职务，也给出林奈那个「居首者」的目。

normal.en: Grasping hands and forward-facing eyes are the usual diagnostic pair.
normal.cn: 抓握的手与朝前的双眼是常用的辨识配对。

normal.en: The family runs primate, primates, Primates, primatology, primatologist, primacy, primal.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 primate、primates、Primates、primatology、primatologist、primacy、primal。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: primate species, primate behaviour, the primate order.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：灵长类物种、灵长类行为、灵长目。

normal.en: Mind the number: Primates is the order, a primate is one of its members.
normal.cn: 注意数：首字母大写的复数是目名，单数形式才是其中一个成员。

abstract.en: Picture an eye that looks forward and a hand that can hold what the eye has chosen.
abstract.cn: 想象一只朝前看的眼，与一只拿得住眼睛所选之物的手。

abstract.en: Picture a bishop and a lemur sharing one word without ever meeting.
abstract.cn: 想象一位主教与一只狐猴共用一个词，却永不相见。

abstract.en: Picture a whole order named after being first, though nobody said first in what.
abstract.cn: 想象整个目因「第一」得名，却没人说是在什么上第一。

examples.en: The primate order includes humans, which is why the name once caused offence.
examples.cn: 灵长目包含人类，这正是这个名称曾引起不快的原因。

examples.en: Primate behaviour is studied at long-term field sites more than in cages.
examples.cn: 灵长类行为更多在长期野外站点研究，而非在笼中。

examples.en: The primate of the province wore the same title as the animal on the poster.
examples.cn: 教省的首席主教与海报上那只动物带着同一个头衔。

dict_mnemonic.text: prim（第一）+ ate＝ 居首者；动物学借林奈之名指「居首的目」；记「一双朝前的眼，一只能握的手」。

root: 拉丁 primas「居首者」，来自 primus「第一」；林奈于 1758 年以 Primates 命名该目，命名动机来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one Latin word for rank: the zoological member, the laboratory subject, the ecological species, the everyday cousin, the bishop, the attributive label, the order itself, the popular catch-all and the evolutionary grade.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项跟着一个表示位次的拉丁词展开：动物学成员、实验对象、生态物种、口语近亲、主教、定语标签、目本身、通俗统称，以及演化等级。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a forward-looking eye, a hand that can grip, and a tail that can wrap a branch.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只朝前的眼、一只能抓握的手，与一条能缠住树枝的尾巴。

branches.en: RANK BECOMES A TAXON: the order and its member share one stem but not one grammar.
branches.cn: 位次变成分类：目与其成员共享词干，却不共享语法。

branches.en: THE OLDER CAREER: a bishop of the first rank entered English long before the lemurs did.
branches.cn: 更早的履历：居首的主教比狐猴更早进入英语。

branches.en: ANIMAL AS OBJECT: a laboratory subject and an ecological node, two ways of counting the same creature.
branches.cn: 动物作为对象：实验对象与生态节点，是数同一类生物的两种方式。

branches.en: KINSHIP AND CATCH-ALL: the warm word for our relatives, and the broad word for any monkey.
branches.cn: 亲缘与泛称：称近亲时的暖词，与指任何猴的宽词。

branches.en: LABEL AND GRADE: an attributive marker, and a body plan named before its taxon existed.
branches.cn: 标签与等级：定语标记，以及在分类出现之前就已得名的身体方案。

intro.en: Primate is a Latin rank word that turned into a taxonomic label; its stem also builds abstract and temporal words that are easily confused with it.
intro.cn: primate 是一个拉丁位次词，后来变成分类标签；同一词干还构成易与它混淆的抽象词与时间词。

latinIntro.en: Latin primus 'first' supplies primas 'of the first rank'; English adds -ate in the noun, while the same stem with other endings gives primacy, primal and primer.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 primus「第一」提供 primas「居首的」；英语在名词上加 -ate，同一词干换其他词尾则得 primacy、primal、primer。

items.example: The stem is shared by every word in this family.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干被本族各词共用。

items.structure: Latin -atus, noun ending on a rank word
items.example: The ending turns the rank word into a person or a thing.
items.exampleCN: 该词尾把位次词变成人或物。

items.meaning: a chief bishop; a member of the first order
items.example: The noun carries both careers in one spelling.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词用一种拼写承载两段履历。

items.meaning: the order of the first ones
items.example: The capitalized plural is a taxon, not a plural of the animal.
items.exampleCN: 首字母大写的复数是分类单元，不是动物的复数。

items.example: The suffix marks a discipline, not a rank.
items.exampleCN: 该词尾标记学科，而非层级。

items.example: The agent ending marks the person.
items.exampleCN: 施动词尾标记人。

items.example: The abstract noun names a position, not an animal.
items.exampleCN: 抽象名词指位置，而非动物。

items.example: The adjective moved from rank to time.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词从位次转到时间。

items.example: The word names what comes first in learning.
items.exampleCN: 这个词指学习中先来的东西。

items.example: The adjective belongs to the church sense only.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词只属教会义。

latinEntries.meaning: one of the first rank; chief

definition_zh: 资源枯竭；资源耗竭
definition_en: the using up of a natural resource faster than it can be replaced
core_image: 一座原本满溢的仓库逐渐见底，货架上只剩空框
scene: 采空的矿坑边缘堆着废弃设备，原本厚实的矿层只剩薄薄一层。 Years of logging led to resource depletion in the valley.
sceneCN: 这里 resource depletion 指「资源被消耗到所剩无几的状态或过程」（第 1 个义项：可再生或不可再生资源被取用的速度超过补充速度）；句意为多年伐木导致这个山谷的资源枯竭。图中可辨识物件：空矿坑、废弃设备、薄矿层、被砍光的坡地。

pos.zh: 资源枯竭；资源耗竭（不可数）

senses.title: Taking a resource faster than it renews
senses.titleCN: 取用速度快于补充速度
senses.definition: the process of drawing on a natural resource faster than natural processes replace it
senses.definitionCN: 取用自然资源的速度超过自然过程补充它的速度
senses.example: Years of logging led to resource depletion in the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 多年伐木导致这个山谷的资源枯竭。
senses.why: resource names a stock that can be drawn on, and depletion is Latin for emptying out, so the phrase describes a stock being emptied.
senses.whyCN: resource 指可供取用的存量，depletion 是拉丁语「倒空」，因此短语描述存量被倒空。

senses.title: The scarce state reached
senses.definition: the condition in which little of the resource remains available
senses.definitionCN: 资源所剩无几的状态
senses.example: The town faced resource depletion after the wells failed.
senses.exampleCN: 水井干涸后，这座城镇面临资源枯竭。
senses.why: the same phrase can name the process or its end state, so it works both as a verb-like and an adjective-like description.
senses.whyCN: 同一短语既可指过程，也可指终态，因此兼具动词性与形容词性的描述功能。

senses.title: Mining an aquifer
senses.definition: the falling of groundwater levels because pumping exceeds recharge
senses.definitionCN: 抽水量超过补给量导致地下水位下降
senses.example: Wetland drainage caused groundwater resource depletion.
senses.exampleCN: 湿地排水造成地下水资源枯竭。
senses.why: groundwater behaves like a bank account with a slow deposit rate, so pumping is literally withdrawal.
senses.whyCN: 地下水像一个存入很慢的账户，抽水就是字面上的取款。

senses.title: Overharvesting renewable stocks
senses.titleCN: 可再生资源的过度采获
senses.definition: the decline of fish, game or timber when harvest exceeds regrowth
senses.definitionCN: 捕捞或采伐超过再生量时鱼类、猎物或木材的下降
senses.example: The fishery collapsed through resource depletion.
senses.exampleCN: 这片渔场因资源枯竭而崩溃。
senses.why: even a resource that renews can be emptied if the rate of taking outruns the rate of return.
senses.whyCN: 即使是可再生资源，只要取用速率超过回补速率，也会被掏空。

senses.title: Exhausting finite minerals and fuels
senses.titleCN: 耗尽有限的矿产与燃料
senses.definition: the permanent loss of coal, oil or ore deposits that cannot be replaced within human time
senses.definitionCN: 煤、石油或矿藏在人类时间尺度内无法补充的永久减少
senses.example: The report warned of resource depletion in the oil fields.
senses.exampleCN: 报告警告油田存在资源枯竭。
senses.why: for a finite stock, depletion is not a cycle but a one-way countdown.
senses.whyCN: 对有限存量而言，耗竭不是循环，而是单向倒计时。

senses.title: Natural capital in national accounts
senses.titleCN: 国民账户中的自然资本
senses.definition: the decrease in the value of natural capital recorded in economic accounting
senses.definitionCN: 经济核算中记录的自然资本价值下降
senses.example: The treasury booked resource depletion as a loss of national wealth.
senses.exampleCN: 财政部把资源耗竭记为国家财富的损失。
senses.why: economists treat a mine or a forest as capital, so taking it out is depreciation under another name.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家把矿或森林当作资本，取出来就是换了名字的折旧。

senses.title: A strategic alarm
senses.definition: the phrase used in politics and security talk to warn of dependence on scarce supplies
senses.definitionCN: 政治与安全话语中用来警告依赖稀缺供给的说法
senses.example: Resource depletion shaped the country's foreign policy.
senses.exampleCN: 资源枯竭塑造了这个国家的外交政策。
senses.why: when a supply is also a strategic input, emptying it becomes a security question rather than only an environmental one.
senses.whyCN: 当一种供给同时也是战略投入，掏空它就成了安全问题，而不只是环境问题。

senses.title: Draining any shared pool
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：任何共享储备被抽干
senses.definition: the exhaustion of any shared pool, such as attention, trust or talent
senses.definitionCN: 任何共享储备的耗尽，如注意力、信任或人才
senses.example: Constant meetings caused resource depletion in the team's energy.
senses.exampleCN: 不断的会议造成团队精力的资源枯竭。
senses.why: the metaphor needs only a common stock and too many withdrawals, which is why it fits organisations as well as aquifers.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻只需一个公共存量与过多的抽取，因此既适用于含水层，也适用于组织。

intro.en: Resource depletion joins resource, from Old French ressource 'a new springing up', with depletion, from Latin deplere 'to empty out'. The modern environmental phrase is recent. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: resource depletion 把 resource（来自古法语 ressource「重新涌出」）与 depletion（来自拉丁 deplere「倒空」）组合起来。现代的环保短语出现较晚。年代均为约数。

items.en: Re- 'again' plus surgere 'to rise' produced resurgere 'to rise again', the source of the idea of a supply that springs back.
items.cn: re-「再次」加 surgere「升起」构成 resurgere「再起」，这是「供给会重新涌出」这一观念的来源。

items.en: Ressource first meant 'a means of recovery, recourse'; the sense of a stock or supply developed later in English.
items.cn: ressource 最初意为「恢复的手段、求助对象」；「储备、资源」义在英语中较晚才发展出来。

items.en: De- 'completely' plus plere 'to fill' gave deplere 'to empty out', literally to un-fill a container.
items.cn: de-「完全」加 plere「装满」构成 deplere「倒空」，字面上就是把容器里的东西卸掉。

items.en: English depletion first described emptying the body of fluids in medicine, then any exhausting of a stock.
items.cn: 英语 depletion 最初在医学中描述排出体液，后来指任何存量的耗尽。

items.en: Resource depletion became a fixed environmental phrase in the twentieth century with the conservation and limits-to-growth debates.
items.cn: resource depletion 在 20 世纪随着资源保护与增长极限的讨论成为固定的环保短语。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the exact first printed use of the phrase is not recorded, and the shift from 'recourse' to 'stock' in resource is gradual rather than dated to one text.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：这个短语确切的最早书证没有记录，而 resource 从「求助」到「存量」的转变是渐进的，无法归到某一文本。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same plere or resource stock that are easily confused; group two holds terms for running a supply down.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 plere 或 resource 词干、容易混淆的词；第二组是描述供给被耗尽的术语。

entries.definition: The process of emptying any stock; resource depletion adds what kind of stock is being emptied.
entries.definitionCN: 任何存量被倒空的过程；resource depletion 补充了被倒空的是哪类存量。

entries.definition: From re- 'again' plus plere 'to fill': the state of being filled again, literally the reverse of depletion.
entries.definitionCN: re-「再次」加 plere「装满」：再次被填满的状态，字面上是 depletion 的反面。

entries.definition: To fill a stock again; it is the action that prevents depletion.
entries.definitionCN: 把存量重新填满；正是防止耗竭的动作。

entries.definition: The verb for emptying a stock; the noun phrase names the resulting process.
entries.definitionCN: 表示倒空存量的动词；名词短语命名由此形成的过程。

entries.definition: The state of having nothing left; depletion can describe partial drawing down as well as the end.
entries.definitionCN: 什么都不剩的状态；depletion 既可指部分下降，也可指终局。

entries.definition: A condition of insufficient supply relative to demand, which depletion produces but does not name directly.
entries.definitionCN: 供给相对需求不足的状态，耗竭会造成它，但并不直接命名它。

entries.definition: Taking a renewable stock beyond its growth rate; it is the behaviour that drives depletion.
entries.definitionCN: 取用可再生存量超过其增长率；这是驱动耗竭的行为。

entries.definition: The measured drop in a stored supply, such as an aquifer's water level; depletion is the broader process.
entries.definitionCN: 储存供给测得的下降，如含水层水位；depletion 是更宽的过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: de- 'completely' + plere 'fill': depletion is un-filling, emptying a container to the bottom.
normal.cn: de-「完全」+ plere「装满」：depletion 就是卸空，把容器倒到底。

normal.en: re- 'again' + plere 'fill': replenish is the exact opposite action.
normal.cn: re-「再次」+ plere「装满」：replenish 正是相反的动作。

normal.en: The family runs deplete, depletion, depleted, replenish, repletion.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 deplete、depletion、depleted、replenish、repletion。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: groundwater resource depletion, resource depletion rate.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：地下水资源枯竭、资源耗竭速率。

normal.en: Resource first meant 'a way to recover', so depletion of a resource is the loss of a fallback.
normal.cn: resource 最初指「恢复的办法」，因此资源枯竭就是退路的丧失。

abstract.en: Picture a warehouse whose shelves are all empty boxes.
abstract.cn: 想象一座仓库，架子上全是空盒子。

abstract.en: Picture a well that echoes back instead of filling.
abstract.cn: 想象一口井，回给你的是回声而不是水。

abstract.en: Picture a shared account drained by too many cards.
abstract.cn: 想象一个共享账户被太多张卡取空。

examples.en: Resource depletion forced the mine to close within a decade.
examples.cn: 资源枯竭迫使这座矿在十年内关闭。

examples.en: The island suffers resource depletion because its wells recharge slowly.
examples.cn: 这座岛的水井补给缓慢，因此遭受资源枯竭。

examples.en: Accounting for resource depletion changes the country's true savings rate.
examples.cn: 把资源耗竭计入账目会改变该国的真实储蓄率。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「resource（资源）+ depletion（倒空）」——资源被倒空 → 资源枯竭

root: resource 来自古法语 ressource，再上溯拉丁 resurgere「再起」= re-「再次」+ surgere「升起」；depletion 来自拉丁 deplere「倒空」= de-「完全」+ plere「装满」。两组词根方向相反。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one stock: a supply is full, it is drawn down, renewal cannot keep pace, the level falls, and the same phrase then names the state, specific aquifers, fish and ore, a national account, a security alarm and finally any shared pool.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个存量展开：储备是满的、被抽取、补充跟不上、水位下降，随后同一短语用来命名状态、具体含水层、鱼类与矿石、国民账户、安全警报，最后指任何共享储备。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a warehouse that was full and is now reduced to empty frames.
core.cn: 核心意象：曾经满溢的仓库如今只剩空货架。

branches.en: PROCESS AND ACCOUNT: taking out exceeds putting back, and treasuries book the fall as lost capital.
branches.cn: 过程与账目：取出超过放回，财政部门把下降记为资本损失。

branches.en: STATE AND ALARM: the remaining stock is small, and politics reads that as dependence and danger.
branches.cn: 状态与警报：剩余存量很少，政治把这一点读作依赖与危险。

branches.en: FINITE STORES: groundwater, coal and ore have no human-scale replacement, so depletion is a countdown.
branches.cn: 有限存量：地下水、煤与矿石在人类尺度上无替代，因此耗竭是倒计时。

branches.en: RENEWABLE OVERHARVEST: fish and timber can renew, but only if harvest stays below regrowth.
branches.cn: 可再生资源的过度采获：鱼类与木材能再生，但前提是采获低于再生量。

branches.en: METAPHOR: attention, trust and talent behave like aquifers when withdrawals outrun recovery.
branches.cn: 比喻：当抽取超过恢复，注意力、信任与人才就像含水层一样。

intro.en: Resource depletion is a phrase of two Latin-derived nouns. The first traces to a verb of rising, the second to a verb of filling, so the two halves pull in opposite directions.
intro.cn: resource depletion 是两个拉丁来源名词构成的短语。前者上溯到「升起」的动词，后者上溯到「装满」的动词，因此两半方向相反。

latinIntro.en: Latin surgere 'to rise' gives resource and surge; Latin plere 'to fill' gives deplete, depletion, replete and replenish.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 surgere「升起」衍生 resource 与 surge；拉丁 plere「装满」衍生 deplete、depletion、replete 与 replenish。

items.example: The prefix adds the idea of springing up again.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀增添「再次涌起」的意思。

items.example: The root supplies the image of a spring.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供泉水的意象。

items.meaning: a means of recovery; a stock
items.example: The forest is a slow resource.
items.exampleCN: 森林是一种恢复缓慢的资源。

items.example: The prefix pushes the filling out of the container.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把填充物推出容器。
这个词根关乎满与不满。
抽水会耗尽含水层。

items.example: Depletion is the result of emptying.
items.exampleCN: depletion 就是倒空的结果。
降雨补充水库。

items.example: Years of logging led to resource depletion in the valley.
items.exampleCN: 多年伐木导致这个山谷的资源枯竭。

definition_zh: n. 双筒望远镜（常用复数形式）
definition_en: a pair of short telescopes joined together, held to both eyes to view distant things
core_image: 双手举着两只并排的镜筒，远处的船一下子被拉到眼前
scene: 他举起双筒望远镜，观察对岸的鸟。 He raised the binoculars to watch the birds on the far shore.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：binoculars 指双手举起的双筒望远镜；句意是他举起望远镜观察对岸的鸟。

forms.label: 固定复数形式（作单件器具）

senses.title: A two-tube viewing instrument
senses.definition: an optical instrument with two parallel tubes, held to both eyes to magnify distant objects
senses.definitionCN: 两管并排、贴双眼观看以放大远处物体的光学器具
senses.example: From the ridge she could follow the whole valley with binoculars.
senses.exampleCN: 从山脊上，她用望远镜能把整条山谷看得清楚。
senses.why: Binocular comes from Latin bini, two at a time, and oculus, eye: an instrument for two eyes.
senses.whyCN: binocular 源自拉丁语 bini（成双）与 oculus（眼）：供双眼使用的器具。

senses.title: A small pair for indoor use
senses.definition: a compact pair with low magnification, used at theatres and concerts
senses.definitionCN: 低倍率、在剧院与音乐会使用的小型双筒镜
senses.example: He kept opera binoculars in his coat for the second act.
senses.exampleCN: 他在外套里放着一副观剧小望远镜，留着第二幕用。
senses.why: The same design is scaled down until it fits a pocket, and the purpose changes with the size.
senses.whyCN: 同样的构造缩小到能放进衣袋，用途便随尺寸改变。

intro.en: Binoculars joins Latin bini, two at a time, to oculus, eye.
intro.cn: binoculars 把拉丁语 bini（成双）与 oculus（眼）连在一起。

items.en: Oculus means eye and stands behind ocular and binocular.
items.cn: oculus 意为眼睛，是 ocular 与 binocular 的词根。

items.en: Bini means two at a time, the distributive form of two.
items.cn: bini 意为「每次两个」，是「二」的分配数词。

items.en: Binoculus describes something with two eyes.
items.cn: binoculus 形容有两只眼睛的东西。

items.en: English binocular appears first as an adjective.
items.cn: 英语 binocular 先作形容词出现。

items.en: Two-tube field glasses become standard for soldiers and sailors.
items.cn: 双筒野外镜成为士兵与水手的标准装备。

items.en: The plural noun settles as the everyday name.
items.cn: 复数名词形式固定为日常称谓。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the ocular build; the near-meaning group runs from the plain instrument to the words for specialised viewing devices.
note.cn: 形近组共享 ocular 构造；近义组从普通器具排到专门用途的观看装置。

entries.definition: Relating to both eyes.
entries.definitionCN: 与双眼有关的。

entries.definition: Relating to a single eye.
entries.definitionCN: 与单眼有关的。

entries.definition: Relating to the eye.
entries.definitionCN: 与眼睛有关的。

entries.definition: Glasses with two lens strengths.
entries.definitionCN: 双焦点眼镜。

entries.definition: An instrument that magnifies distant objects.
entries.definitionCN: 放大远处物体的器具。

entries.definition: A small telescope held in one hand.
entries.definitionCN: 单手可持的小型望远镜。

entries.definition: An old term for a pair of binoculars.
entries.definitionCN: 双筒望远镜的旧称。

entries.definition: Any instrument for looking through.
entries.definitionCN: 任何用于窥看的器具。

normalIntro.en: Bini is two at a time and oculus is eye, so binoculars are simply two eyes of glass.
normalIntro.cn: bini 意为成双，oculus 意为眼，binoculars 就是两只玻璃做的眼睛。

normal.en: Ocular means of the eye, as in ocular migraine.
normal.cn: ocular 意为眼的，如 ocular migraine（眼型偏头痛）。

normal.en: Bini means two at a time, so bi-nocular is two-eyed.
normal.cn: bini 意为成双，bi-nocular 就是双眼用的。

normal.en: One tube would be a monocular, a single eye.
normal.cn: 只有一管就是 monocular，单眼。

normal.en: The word is plural because there are two tubes.
normal.cn: 用复数形式是因为有两只镜筒。

normal.en: Two glass eyes held up bring the horizon close.
normal.cn: 举起两只玻璃眼，地平线就到了眼前。

abstract.en: Borrowed eyes on a strap.
abstract.cn: 挂在带子上的一双借来的眼睛。

abstract.en: Distance folded into two circles.
abstract.cn: 把距离折进两个圆里。

abstract.en: Attention made into an instrument.
abstract.cn: 把注意力做成一件器具。

examples.en: She scanned the ridge line with her binoculars.
examples.cn: 她用望远镜扫过整条山脊。

examples.en: These binoculars are waterproof and filled with nitrogen.
examples.cn: 这副望远镜防水，内充氮气。

examples.en: He forgot the binoculars and watched the whales with bare eyes.
examples.cn: 他忘了带望远镜，只能用肉眼观看鲸鱼。

dict_mnemonic.text: bi 是「两个」，ocular 是「眼睛」——两个镜筒就是两只玻璃眼，凑到眼前就能望得很远。

root: 拉丁 bini（成双）+ oculus（眼）+ -ar（形容词后缀）+ -s（名词复数）

sensesIntro.en: The instrument and its pocket-sized theatre version share one design; only the scale and the setting change.
sensesIntro.cn: 实用双筒镜与衣袋里的观剧镜共用一种构造，只改变尺寸与场合。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two glass circles lifted to two eyes, and a distant ship jumping close
core.cn: 核心意象：两个玻璃圆片举到眼前，远处的船一下跳到近处

branches.en: A headland swept from end to end.
branches.cn: 从一端扫到另一端的海岬。

branches.en: A bird named at two hundred metres.
branches.cn: 两百米外被认出的鸟。

branches.en: A small pair in a coat pocket.
branches.cn: 外套口袋里的一副小望远镜。

branches.en: A second-act view of the stage.
branches.cn: 第二幕时望向舞台的目光。

branches.en: Two eyes of glass, near or far.
branches.cn: 两只玻璃眼，或近或远。

intro.en: Binoculars is a Latin eye-word wearing English endings; the list below shows the optical family and its tools.
intro.cn: binoculars 是一个拉丁语「眼」词穿上英语词尾；下面列出光学词族与器具词。

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 oculus 意为眼，bini 意为成双，videre 意为看见。
