definition_zh: 数学家；数学工作者；（旧时）占星术士
definition_en: a person who studies or works in mathematics; in earlier English, also a person who practised astrology
core_image: 书房里，一位研究者面前只有几张写满符号的纸，墙上小黑板还留着一条待证的命题
scene: 书房里，一位研究者面前的纸上只有符号与箭头，墙上的小黑板写着一个还没证完的命题。 The mathematician worked for six years before the proof was accepted.
sceneCN: 这里 mathematician 指「以研究数学为业的人」（第 1 个义项：从事数学研究的人）；句意为这位数学家做了六年，证明才被接受。图中可辨识物件：草稿纸、符号、小黑板、铅笔。

pos.zh: （十六、十七世纪用法）占星术士

senses.title: A researcher in mathematics
senses.definition: a person whose profession is to study or advance mathematics
senses.definitionCN: 以研究或推进数学为职业的人
senses.example: The mathematician worked for six years before the proof was accepted.
senses.exampleCN: 这位数学家做了六年，证明才被接受。
senses.why: The person suffix turns the field's name into the name of someone who works in it.
senses.whyCN: 表人后缀把学科之名变成从事该学科者之名。

senses.title: A teacher of the subject
senses.titleCN: 数学教师与数学工作者
senses.definition: a person who teaches mathematics or applies it as part of a job
senses.definitionCN: 教授数学、或在工作中的一部分运用数学的人
senses.example: The school hired a mathematician to run the advanced class.
senses.exampleCN: 学校聘请了一位数学工作者来带高级班。
senses.why: Teaching and applied work both count as living by the subject, so the word covers more than research alone.
senses.whyCN: 教书与应用工作都算靠这门学问谋生，因此这个词的覆盖面大于纯研究。

senses.title: Someone good with numbers
senses.titleCN: 擅长计算的人（宽泛说法）
senses.definition: used loosely of anyone unusually skilled at calculation
senses.definitionCN: 宽松地指任何在计算上特别熟练的人
senses.example: You do not need to be a mathematician to check that bill.
senses.exampleCN: 核对那张账单并不需要你是数学家。
senses.why: Everyday speech uses the word as a compliment for number sense, without insisting on formal training.
senses.whyCN: 日常说法用这个词称赞数字感，并不要求受过正式训练。

senses.title: A specialist in one branch
senses.definition: a person expert in a particular branch, such as geometry or number theory
senses.definitionCN: 精通某一分支（如几何或数论）的人
senses.example: The geometer and the analyst were both mathematicians, but they read different journals.
senses.exampleCN: 几何学家与分析学家都是数学家，但读的期刊不同。
senses.why: Branch names describe narrower expertise while the general word still applies to all of them.
senses.whyCN: 分支名称描述更窄的专长，而通名仍适用于其中所有人。

senses.title: A historical author of mathematical works
senses.titleCN: 历史上撰写数学著作的人
senses.definition: a historical figure known for written mathematical work rather than for a modern post
senses.definitionCN: 以数学著述而非现代职位闻名的历史人物
senses.example: The mathematician left a single book that was read for centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 这位数学家只留下一本书，却被读了几个世纪。
senses.why: History remembers people by their books, so the word attaches to authorship as much as to employment.
senses.whyCN: 历史按著作记住人，因此这个词既指职业，也指著述身份。

senses.title: An astrologer, in older usage
senses.definition: in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, a person who cast horoscopes and calculated celestial positions
senses.definitionCN: 在十六、十七世纪，指推算星盘与天体位置的人
senses.example: In Shakespeare's day a mathematician might be paid to read the stars.
senses.exampleCN: 在莎士比亚的时代，「数学家」可能受雇去读星象。
senses.why: Astronomy and astrology were then one body of calculation, and whoever did that calculation carried the name.
senses.whyCN: 当时天文与占星是一套计算，做这套计算的人便带着这个名号。

senses.title: A modeller in industry
senses.titleCN: 工业与金融中的数学建模人员
senses.definition: a person employed to build mathematical models for practical decisions
senses.definitionCN: 受雇为实际决策建立数学模型的人
senses.example: The insurer's mathematicians priced the new policy.
senses.exampleCN: 这家保险公司的数学人员为新保单定了价。
senses.why: Outside academia the same training is sold as modelling, and the old word follows the skill.
senses.whyCN: 在学界之外，同样的训练以建模之名出售，旧词随技能而行。

senses.title: A calculating person, figuratively
senses.definition: used of someone who plans every move as if solving an equation
senses.definitionCN: 比喻把每一步都当作解方程来筹划的人
senses.example: A good negotiator is something of a mathematician about other people's motives.
senses.exampleCN: 好的谈判者对他人动机的把握颇有几分数学家的味道。
senses.why: The figurative use transfers the cool step-by-step manner of proof to social behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 比喻用法把证明中那种冷静的逐步骤态度移用到社交行为上。

intro.en: The word is the name of the field plus a suffix for a person. Its Greek root means 'learning', and its early English sense could include astrology. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词由学科之名加表人后缀构成。其希腊词根意为「学习」，早期英语中还可指占星。年代均为约数。

items.en: Mathēma 'something learned' came from manthanein 'to learn'; the deeper root is reconstructed, not attested.
items.cn: mathēma「所学之物」源自动词 manthanein「学习」；更深词根属重构形式，并无实证。

items.en: Latin mathematicus named a student of the mathematical studies, and in later usage could also mean an astrologer.
items.cn: 拉丁 mathematicus 指数学诸科的研习者，后世也可指占星者。

items.en: Sixteenth-century English used mathematic for the field itself, and the person's name was formed from it.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语用 mathematic 指这门学问本身，表人之名即由此构成。

items.en: The ending came into English through French from Latin -ianus, which marks someone connected with a thing.
items.cn: 这个表人词尾经法语来自拉丁 -ianus，标记与某事物有关联的人。

items.en: Because celestial prediction was then a branch of calculation, a mathematician could be hired to cast a horoscope; the sense faded as the two trades separated.
items.cn: 由于当时星象预测属于计算的一支，「数学家」可受雇推算星盘；随着两种行业分开，这一义项衰落。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the word settled on the academic and industrial researcher. First date uncertain: no single year is recorded for the narrower modern sense.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，这个词固定指学术与工业中的研究者。首见年代不确定：较窄的现代义没有确切年份记录。

note.en: Group one separates words that look alike but belong to different roots; group two separates the neighbouring specialists.
note.cn: 第一组辨析外形相近而词根不同的词；第二组辨析相邻的专门从业者。

entries.definition: An older adjective and singular noun for the field; it never names a person, though it looks like a shortened form of this word.
entries.definitionCN: 更早的形容词与单数名词，指这门学问；它从不指人，尽管看起来像本词的缩短形式。

entries.definition: Describes work or ability rather than a person; 'a mathematical person' is not the same as 'a mathematician'.
entries.definitionCN: 描述工作或能力，而不指人；「有数学头脑的人」与「数学家」并不等同。

entries.definition: A person skilled in arithmetic, built on the Greek word for number rather than on the word for learning.
entries.definitionCN: 指精通算术的人，建立在希腊语表示数字的词上，而非表示学习的词上。

entries.definition: A specialist in geometry; the branch name plus the person suffix, parallel in form but narrower in scope.
entries.definitionCN: 指几何学专家；分支名加表人后缀，形式平行而范围更窄。

entries.definition: One who works mainly with symbolic equations; a mathematician may never touch algebra.
entries.definitionCN: 主要指从事符号方程工作的人；数学家未必接触代数。

entries.definition: An older and more formal word for a worker in geometry, still used for classical studies of shape.
entries.definitionCN: 指几何工作者的更旧更正式的说法，仍用于对形的古典研究。

entries.definition: One who works with data and probability; the training overlaps but the daily work differs.
entries.definitionCN: 指处理数据与概率的人；训练有重叠，但日常工作不同。

entries.definition: One who calculates risk and premiums for insurers, using mathematics as a tool rather than as a subject.
entries.definitionCN: 指为保险机构计算风险与保费的人，把数学当工具而非研究对象。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The word is the field's name plus a person suffix, so it means one who lives by the field.
normal.cn: 这个词是学科名加表人后缀，因此指靠这门学问谋生的人。

normal.en: The Greek root says 'learned', so the earliest bearers of the name were simply people of learning.
normal.cn: 希腊词根意为「有学问的」，因此最早带这个名号的人只是有学问者。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the roles: pure mathematician, applied mathematician, a team of mathematicians.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出角色：纯数学家、应用数学家、一组数学家。

normal.en: In Shakespeare's time the same word could mean an astrologer, since star-reading was then calculation.
normal.cn: 在莎士比亚时代，同一个词可指占星者，因为读星象当时属于计算。

normal.en: The family runs mathematics, mathematical, mathematician, mathematically, plus the old form mathematic.
normal.cn: 同族词包括数学、数学的、数学家、在数学上，另有旧形式「数学的」。

abstract.en: Picture a person who fills a wall with a single proof and then sleeps beside it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人把一整面墙写满同一个证明，然后就在旁边睡下。

abstract.en: Picture a locksmith who never touches a door but knows every lock in the city.
abstract.cn: 想象一位锁匠从不碰门，却熟悉全城每一把锁。

abstract.en: Picture a chess player who sees the board three moves before anyone else does.
abstract.cn: 想象一位棋手，比旁人早三步看见棋盘。

examples.en: The mathematician published the proof in a journal read by few.
examples.cn: 这位数学家把证明发表在一份读者很少的期刊上。

examples.en: Applied mathematicians now work closely with surgeons.
examples.cn: 应用数学家如今与外科医生密切合作。

examples.en: As a mathematician she distrusted any argument that skipped a step.
examples.cn: 作为数学家，她不信任任何跳过一步的论证。

dict_mnemonic.text: 记作「学数学的人」：学科名换上一个表人尾巴 → 数学家

root: 希腊 mathēma「所学之物」+ 拉丁 -ianus 表人后缀（经法语入英语）；拉丁 mathematicus 兼指数学研习者与占星者；十六、十七世纪英语中可指占星术士，十九世纪固定为现代数学家。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the researcher to the teacher, the number-skilled person, the branch specialist, the historical author, the old astrologer, the industrial modeller, and finally the calculating character of a negotiator.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从研究者，移到教师、擅长数字者、分支专家、历史著作者、旧时的占星者、工业建模者，最后到谈判者身上那种精于算计的气质。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a desk with symbol-covered pages and a small board holding an unfinished proof.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张桌子，上面是写满符号的纸，旁边小黑板留着未完成的证明。

branches.en: Research and teaching: the same training spent either on new proofs or on other people's lessons.
branches.cn: 研究与教学：同样的训练，或用于新证明，或用于他人的课。

branches.en: Number sense, plain and figurative: a compliment at a till, a metaphor at a negotiating table.
branches.cn: 数字感，字面与比喻：收银台边的称赞，谈判桌上的隐喻。

branches.en: The narrow branch and the remembered book: expertise can be local or historical.
branches.cn: 窄分支与留存的书：专长可以是局部的，也可以是历史的。

branches.en: The old stars: the same name once covered those who read horoscopes.
branches.cn: 旧时的星：同一个名号曾涵盖读星盘的人。

branches.en: The market: the same skill sold as modelling for insurers and engineers.
branches.cn: 市场：同样的技能作为建模卖给保险与工程。

intro.en: The word is a Greek stem with a Greek adjective suffix, then a Latin person suffix, all of which also build the rest of the family.
intro.cn: 这个词是希腊词干加希腊形容词后缀，再加拉丁表人后缀，这些部件也构成词族其余部分。

latinIntro.en: Greek mathēma supplies 'learning', -ikos marks belonging, and Latin -ianus (through French) marks a person.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语名词提供「学习」之义，希腊后缀标记「属于」，拉丁后缀经法语标记人。

items.example: The stem supplies the learning at the heart of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干提供词心处的「学问」。

items.example: The suffix turns the noun into the adjective from which the person name is built.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成形容词，再由它构成表人之名。

items.example: The Greek adjective is the base of the English noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊形容词是英语名词的基础。

items.example: The Latin suffix marks a person associated with the field.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁后缀标记与该领域有关的人。

items.example: The English ending is the everyday person marker for trades and fields.
items.exampleCN: 这个英语词尾是行业与领域的常用表人标记。

items.example: The word names the practitioner rather than the practice.
items.exampleCN: 这个词指从业者而非这门实践。

items.example: The field name is what the person name is built on.
items.exampleCN: 表人之名建立在学科名上。

items.example: The adjective describes the work rather than the worker.
items.exampleCN: 形容词描述工作而非工作者。

items.example: The adverb marks the manner of working.
items.exampleCN: 副词标记工作的方式。

latinEntries.structure: mathēma, mathēmatos (n., third declension, Greek loan)

definition_zh: 结晶；结晶作用；（计划、想法等的）具体化、明确成形
definition_en: the process by which crystals form from a solution or a melt, or the process by which an idea becomes definite
core_image: 糖厂车间里，浓缩糖浆在搅拌槽中冷却，槽壁上结出密密一层白色糖粒
scene: 糖厂车间里，浓缩的糖浆倒进搅拌槽，冷却后槽壁上结出密密的一层糖粒。 Slow cooling and stirring promote crystallization of the sugar.
sceneCN: 这里 crystallization 指「溶质从溶液或熔体中析出、长成晶体的过程」（第 1 个义项：结晶作用）；句意为缓慢冷却与搅拌促进糖的结晶。可辨识物件：搅拌槽、浓缩糖浆、槽壁糖粒、冷却夹套。

senses.title: Formation of crystals from liquid
senses.titleCN: 从液体中长出晶体的过程
senses.definition: the process by which ordered crystals separate from a solution or a melt
senses.definitionCN: 指有序晶体从溶液或熔体中析出的过程
senses.example: Slow cooling and stirring promote crystallization of the sugar.
senses.exampleCN: 缓慢冷却与搅拌促进糖的结晶。
senses.why: -ation names the process, and the definition is the formation of ordered solid from liquid.
senses.whyCN: -ation 命名过程，定义即有序固体从液体中形成。

senses.title: Crystallization of magma
senses.definition: the geological process in which minerals crystallize from cooling magma
senses.definitionCN: 指矿物从冷却岩浆中结晶的地质过程
senses.example: Crystallization of the magma began with olivine.
senses.exampleCN: 岩浆的结晶从橄榄石开始。
senses.why: Magma is a melt, so its mineral growth is the geological case of the same process.
senses.whyCN: 岩浆是一种熔体，其矿物生长是同一过程的地质情形。

senses.title: Purification by crystallization
senses.definition: the use of repeated crystal formation to remove impurities from a substance
senses.definitionCN: 指反复结晶以除去杂质
senses.example: Repeated crystallization removed the last traces of salt.
senses.exampleCN: 反复结晶除去了最后一点盐。
senses.why: Repeated growth excludes impurities, which is what purification by crystallization means.
senses.whyCN: 反复生长排除杂质，这正是结晶提纯的含义。

senses.title: Controlled crystallization in industry
senses.definition: the controlled production of crystals of a chosen size in food or chemical plants
senses.definitionCN: 指在食品或化工厂中控制晶体尺寸的生产过程
senses.example: The factory controls crystallization to fix the grain size.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂控制结晶以固定晶粒尺寸。
senses.why: Industry controls temperature and stirring to fix grain size.
senses.whyCN: 工业控制温度与搅拌，以固定晶粒尺寸。

senses.title: Fractional crystallization
senses.definition: a separation method in which substances crystallize one after another as temperature falls
senses.definitionCN: 指随温度下降而使不同物质先后结晶的分离方法
senses.example: Fractional crystallization separated the two salts.
senses.exampleCN: 分步结晶把两种盐分离开。
senses.why: Different substances crystallize at different temperatures, which makes separation possible.
senses.whyCN: 不同物质在不同温度结晶，这才使分离成为可能。

senses.title: Ice crystallization
senses.definition: the formation of ice crystals in water, food or living tissue
senses.definitionCN: 指水、食品或活组织中冰晶的形成
senses.example: Ice crystallization cracked the water pipe.
senses.exampleCN: 冰的结晶把水管胀裂了。
senses.why: Water is a melt of ice, and its crystals form in cells and pipes.
senses.whyCN: 水是冰的熔体，其晶体在细胞与管道中形成。

senses.title: Becoming definite
senses.definition: the process by which plans, ideas or movements take a clear and fixed form
senses.definitionCN: 指计划、想法或运动取得清晰固定形态的过程
senses.example: The plan's crystallization took two years of talks.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划用了两年谈判才成形。
senses.why: The metaphor treats an idea as a dissolved thing that becomes solid and definite.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把想法当作溶解之物，逐渐变硬、变明确。

senses.title: A concrete embodiment
senses.definition: the definite result in which an idea or tendency becomes visible and fixed
senses.definitionCN: 指使想法或趋势变得可见、固定的具体成果
senses.example: The treaty was the crystallization of a long rivalry.
senses.exampleCN: 这项条约是长期对抗的具体结晶。
senses.why: The definite result is the embodiment, the last step of the same image.
senses.whyCN: 明确的结果就是具体化身，是同一意象的最后一步。

intro.en: Crystallization is crystal turned into a process noun by two Latin-descended suffixes, -ize and -ation.
intro.cn: crystallization 由 crystal 加两个拉丁来源后缀 -ize 与 -ation 构成过程名词。

items.en: Krystallos 'ice, rock crystal' passed through Latin crystallus into English crystal.
items.cn: krystallos「冰、水晶」经拉丁 crystallus 进入英语 crystal。

items.en: Latin -izare and Greek -izein formed verbs meaning 'to make, to become'; English -ize builds verbs such as crystallize.
items.cn: 拉丁 -izare 与希腊 -izein 构成表示「使……、成为……」的动词；英语 -ize 构成 crystallize 这类动词。

items.en: Latin -atio, -ationis names an action or process, so crystallization is the process, not one crystal.
items.cn: 拉丁 -atio、-ationis 命名动作或过程，因此 crystallization 指过程，而非某一颗晶体。

items.en: In the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries the noun became standard in chemistry for purification and in geology for the growth of minerals from magma.
items.cn: 在十八、十九世纪，这个名词在化学中成为提纯的标准说法，在地质学中则指矿物从岩浆中生长。

items.en: Sugar refining gave the word a mass-production sense, and from the nineteenth century it was also used of ideas taking definite shape.
items.cn: 制糖业给这个词带来大批量生产的意义；从十九世纪起，它也被用于想法取得明确形态。

items.en: Not uncertain: the suffixal derivation is established. Only the first date of the figurative sense is approximate, and the Greek origin of krystallos is discussed under crystal.
items.cn: 并非存疑：后缀派生是确定的。仅比喻义的首次年代为约数，krystallos 的希腊来源见 crystal 词条。

note.en: Group one holds -ization words and family forms that look alike; group two holds the physical processes it is confused with.
note.cn: 第一组是外形相近的 -ization 词与同族形式；第二组是易与它混淆的物理过程。

entries.definition: The British spelling with -isation; it is the same word, not a different process.
entries.definitionCN: 英式拼写，用 -isation；是同一个词，不是另一过程。

entries.definition: The study and description of crystal structure, built with -graphy 'writing' rather than -ization 'process'.
entries.definitionCN: 指对晶体结构的研究与描述，后缀是 -graphy「书写」而非 -ization「过程」。

entries.definition: The medical burning of tissue, from Greek kautēr 'branding iron'; it shares the ending only.
entries.definitionCN: 指医学上烧灼组织，来自希腊 kautēr「烙铁」；只共享词尾。

entries.definition: The degree to which a material is crystalline, an abstract property rather than an event.
entries.definitionCN: 指材料结晶的程度，是一种抽象属性而非事件。

entries.definition: The formation of a solid from a solution by reaction; crystallization is ordered growth, precipitation need not be ordered.
entries.definitionCN: 指反应使溶液析出固体；结晶是有序生长，沉淀则不必有序。

entries.definition: The general change from liquid to solid; crystallization is solidification that produces order.
entries.definitionCN: 指由液体变为固体的总过程；结晶是产生秩序的那种凝固。

entries.definition: The change from liquid to solid by cooling, usually of water; crystallization is the wider term.
entries.definitionCN: 指因冷却由液变固，通常指水；crystallization 是更宽的说法。

entries.definition: The formation of the first tiny crystal that later grows; it is the beginning of crystallization, not the whole process.
entries.definitionCN: 指后来会长大的第一个微晶形成；它是结晶的开端，不是全过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real suffix chain and the real industrial and geological settings.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的后缀链与真实的工业、地质场景。

normal.en: Crystal, crystallize, crystallization: the noun of the process, built by -ize and -ation.
normal.cn: crystal、crystallize、crystallization：由 -ize 与 -ation 构成的过程名词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: fractional crystallization, crystallization temperature, water of crystallization.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：分步结晶、结晶温度、结晶水。

normal.en: In a solution, cooling and stirring bring the first nuclei and then growth.
normal.cn: 在溶液里，降温与搅拌先带来晶核，然后是长大。

normal.en: In geology the sequence is olivine, pyroxene, feldspar, quartz, the Bowen series.
normal.cn: 在地质学中顺序是橄榄石、辉石、长石、石英，即鲍文反应系列。

normal.en: The figurative use says a plan crystallizes when it stops being vague.
normal.cn: 比喻用法说计划「结晶」，意思是它不再模糊。

abstract.en: Picture a cloud of dissolved salt deciding where to put its first solid corner.
abstract.cn: 想象一团溶解的盐决定把第一个固体角落放在哪里。

abstract.en: Picture an idea slowly hardening into a building you can walk into.
abstract.cn: 想象一个想法慢慢硬化成一栋可以走进去的建筑。

abstract.en: Picture winter turning a puddle into a floor of tiny panes.
abstract.cn: 想象冬天把水洼变成一层小玻璃板。

examples.en: Fractional crystallization is used to separate salts with different solubilities.
examples.cn: 分步结晶用于分离溶解度不同的盐。

examples.en: The crystallization of magma releases latent heat into the surrounding rock.
examples.cn: 岩浆结晶把潜热释放到周围岩石中。

examples.en: Water of crystallization is lost when the blue crystals are heated.
examples.cn: 加热蓝色晶体时，结晶水会失去。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「克瑞斯（crystal）里（li）扎（za）tion」——晶粒一颗颗扎堆长出来 → 结晶

root: crystal（希腊 krystallos「冰、水晶」）+ -ize（拉丁 -izare / 希腊 -izein，使……）+ -ation（拉丁 -atio，动作名词后缀）→ crystallization「结晶过程」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one process from solution to symbol: crystals nucleate and grow, then do it underground, in a refinery, in a plant, in a separation column, in ice, in a plan and finally in a treaty.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让同一过程从溶液走到象征：晶体成核并长大，然后依次发生在地下、精炼厂、工厂、分离柱、冰里、计划里，最后在条约里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tank wall slowly furred with white grains as the syrup cools.
core.cn: 核心意象：糖浆冷却时，槽壁慢慢结满白色颗粒。

branches.en: FROM LIQUID TO ORDER: water and syrup follow the same nucleation-and-growth path.
branches.cn: 从液体到秩序：水与糖浆走同一条成核—生长路径。

branches.en: UNDERGROUND: magma crystallizes minerals in a fixed sequence as it cools.
branches.cn: 地下：岩浆冷却时按固定顺序结晶出矿物。

branches.en: PURITY AND PRODUCT: repeated growth removes impurities, and controlled growth fixes grain size.
branches.cn: 纯度与产品：反复生长除去杂质，受控生长固定晶粒尺寸。

branches.en: SEPARATION: falling temperature makes different substances crystallize one by one.
branches.cn: 分离：降温使不同物质先后结晶。

branches.en: THE IDEA TAKES SHAPE: what was vague becomes a plan, and then a document.
branches.cn: 想法成形：模糊之物先成为计划，再成为文件。

intro.en: Crystallization stacks a Greek noun with two derivational suffixes, so the whole word reads as 'the process of making crystal'.
intro.cn: crystallization 把一个希腊名词与两个派生后缀叠起来，整词读作「使成晶体的过程」。

latinIntro.en: Latin crystallus (from Greek krystallos) supplies the base; -izare and -atio supply the verb and the process noun, as in organized and organization.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 crystallus（源自希腊 krystallos）提供词基；-izare 与 -atio 提供动词与过程名词，如 organized 与 organization。

items.example: The stem names the ordered solid.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干命名有序固体。

items.example: The suffix turns a noun into a verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成动词。

items.example: The sugar crystallized on the wall.
items.exampleCN: 糖在槽壁上结晶。

items.example: Organization is the act of organizing.
items.exampleCN: organization 是组织这一动作。
结晶提纯了盐。
这层壳是晶质的。
结晶度影响强度。

items.meaning: a vessel in which crystals form
items.exampleCN: 浆料离开结晶器。
晶体学测绘原子位置。

latinEntries.structure: crystallus, crystalli (m., second declension; Greek loan)

definition_zh: 补充物；补足；配套；（语法）补语；（数学）补集；（生物）补体
definition_en: something that completes another thing or makes it whole; to complete by adding what is missing
core_image: 一片拼图正好补进缺口，边线严丝合缝
scene: 餐桌上的深色桌布衬得浅色餐具更亮。 The cool sauce is a complement to the rich meat.
sceneCN: 这里指补足他物、使其完整的东西（第 1 个义项：补足物）；句意为这清爽的酱汁与厚重的肉相配，正好补足。

pos.zh: 补充物；补足物；配套物；补语；补集；补体

senses.title: Something that completes another thing
senses.definition: a thing that supplies what another thing lacks
senses.definitionCN: 补上另一物所缺之物的东西
senses.example: The cool sauce is a complement to the rich meat.
senses.exampleCN: 这清爽的酱汁与厚重的肉相配。
senses.why: Complementum is that which fills up, from complere, to fill completely.
senses.whyCN: complementum 指把东西填满的部分，出自 complere「完全填满」。

senses.title: To complete by adding
senses.definition: to add what is needed to make something whole
senses.definitionCN: 加上所需之物使某事物完整
senses.example: The two parts complement each other.
senses.exampleCN: 这两部分相互补足。
senses.why: The verb turns the filling into an act performed by one thing on another.
senses.whyCN: 动词把「填满」变成一物对另一物施行的动作。

senses.title: A matched set
senses.definition: the full number needed for a set or a ship's crew
senses.definitionCN: 一个组合或一艘船所需的全额人数
senses.example: The ship sailed with its full complement of crew.
senses.exampleCN: 这艘船载着全额船员出海。
senses.why: A set is complete when its count is filled, and the word marks that count.
senses.whyCN: 一个组合在人数填满时才算完整，这个词标记那个数额。

senses.title: A grammatical complement
senses.definition: a word or phrase that completes the meaning of a verb or subject
senses.definitionCN: 补足动词或主语意义的词或短语
senses.example: In the sentence she is a doctor, the noun is a complement.
senses.exampleCN: 在「她是一名医生」这句话里，那个名词是补语。
senses.why: Grammar borrowed the filling image for the part that makes a clause whole.
senses.whyCN: 语法学借「填充」意象，指使从句完整的部分。

senses.title: A mathematical complement
senses.definition: the set of elements not in a given set
senses.definitionCN: 不属于某集合的元素所成的集合
senses.example: The complement of the odd numbers is the even numbers.
senses.exampleCN: 奇数的补集是偶数。
senses.why: Set theory asks what is left when a part is taken away, and calls it the filling of the rest.
senses.whyCN: 集合论问取走一部分后剩下什么，并把剩余称为补。

senses.title: A part of the immune system
senses.definition: a group of proteins that help antibodies destroy pathogens
senses.definitionCN: 协助抗体消灭病原体的一组蛋白
senses.example: The complement system marks the bacterium for destruction.
senses.exampleCN: 补体系统给细菌做上待清除的标记。
senses.why: The name was given because the proteins complete the work of antibodies.
senses.whyCN: 得名是因为这些蛋白完成抗体的工作。

senses.title: A colour opposite
senses.definition: a colour that sits opposite another on the colour wheel
senses.definitionCN: 色轮上与另一色相对的颜色
senses.example: Blue and orange are complementary colours.
senses.exampleCN: 蓝与橙是互补色。
senses.why: Two opposites complete a neutral balance, so the word fits the pair.
senses.whyCN: 两个相反色合成中性平衡，因此这个词适用于这一对。

senses.title: A logical complement
senses.definition: the negation or remainder of a proposition or class
senses.definitionCN: 命题或类别的否定或剩余
senses.example: The complement of the claim covers every other case.
senses.exampleCN: 这一说法的补覆盖其余所有情况。
senses.why: Logic uses the word for whatever the first statement leaves outside it.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑学用这个词指第一个陈述留在其外的一切。

intro.en: Complement comes from Latin complementum, that which fills up, from complere, to fill completely, built on com- together and plere, to fill. The direct source is clear.
intro.cn: complement 来自拉丁 complementum「用来填满之物」，出自 complere「完全填满」，由 com-「一起」与 plere「填」构成。直接来源清楚。

items.en: Plere meant to fill, and it also lies behind complete, supply and plenty.
items.cn: plere 意为填满，也藏在 complete、supply 与 plenty 背后。

items.en: Complere joined com- together with plere, giving the sense of filling something to the full.
items.cn: complere 把 com-「一起」与 plere 结合，给出「填到满」的意思。

items.en: Complementum was the part that did the filling, the thing needed to make a whole.
items.cn: complementum 指完成填充的那部分，即使整体成立所需之物。

items.en: French passed the word to English; the exact first English date is uncertain.
items.cn: 法语把这个词传给英语，英语确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Compliment reached English through French and Italian courtesy, and though both lines end at complere, the two words separated early.
items.cn: compliment 经法语与意大利语的礼节用法进入英语；两条线虽都止于 complere，词却很早分道。

items.en: Grammar, set theory, immunology and colour theory each name their missing piece a complement.
items.cn: 语法、集合论、免疫学与色彩理论都把自己缺的那一块叫作补。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin filling stem; the second group names things that complete or go well with another.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「填满」词干；第二组是补足或相配的近义说法。

entries.definition: Praise or a polite remark; a different word despite the closeness.
entries.definitionCN: 称赞或礼貌用语；虽形近却是另一个词。

entries.definition: Serving to complete or balance another thing.
entries.definitionCN: 起补足或平衡另一物作用的。

entries.definition: The act or process of completing.
entries.definitionCN: 补足的行为或过程。

entries.definition: Whole, with nothing missing; from the same filling verb.
entries.definitionCN: 完整的，什么都不缺；出自同一「填满」动词。

entries.definition: To provide what is needed; from supplere, to fill up.
entries.definitionCN: 提供所需之物；出自 supplere「填满」。

entries.definition: Something added to improve or extend, not to complete.
entries.definitionCN: 为改进或延长而添加之物，不是为补全。

entries.definition: A person or thing matching another in role.
entries.definitionCN: 在角色上与他者对应的人或物。

entries.definition: Something put in beside what is already there.
entries.definitionCN: 放到已有之物旁边的东西。

entries.definition: One of a pair that goes well with the other.
entries.definitionCN: 与另一件相配的一件。

entries.definition: An even arrangement of opposite parts.
entries.definitionCN: 相反部分之间的均衡安排。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin filling verb, the real family and real collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁「填满」动词、真实同族词与真实搭配。

normal.en: Complere is to fill completely, so a complement is the piece that fills the gap.
normal.cn: complere 是完全填满，所以 complement 就是填缺口的那一块。

normal.en: Complement completes; supplement adds without necessarily completing.
normal.cn: complement 补全；supplement 添加，却未必补全。

normal.en: Compliment is praise, not completion, even though the two words look alike.
normal.cn: compliment 是称赞，不是补全，尽管两个词长得像。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the use: a complement to, full complement, complement each other.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：对…的补充、全额编制、相互补足。

normal.en: Set theory and immunology both name their missing piece a complement.
normal.cn: 集合论与免疫学都把自己缺的那一块叫补。

abstract.en: Complement is a puzzle piece whose edge fits exactly, making the picture whole.
abstract.cn: 补充是一块边线正吻合的拼图，让画面完整。

abstract.en: The word does not add more of the same; it adds what was missing.
abstract.cn: 这个词不是添加同类的更多，而是添加缺少的那一种。

abstract.en: Two opposite colours complete each other into grey.
abstract.cn: 两种相反色相互补足成灰。

examples.en: The two sisters have complementary talents but very different habits.
examples.cn: 两姐妹才能互补，习惯却大不相同。

examples.en: A full complement of officers reported for duty.
examples.cn: 全额军官报到履职。

examples.en: The wine complements the cheese without overpowering it.
examples.cn: 这款酒与奶酪相配，却不压过它。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「康普力门特」——把缺的那块补齐：补充；补足物

root: 拉丁 complementum「用来填满之物」← complere「完全填满」← com-「一起」+ plere「填」。同族 complete、supply 同出 plere；compliment 经法语与意大利语礼节用法另成一路，虽同止于 complere 但很早分道。法语传入英语，确切首见年代不确定；语法、集合论、免疫学与色彩理论各有专义。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses fill a gap in table, theory, grammar, sets, immunity, colour, logic and a taste.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项在餐桌、理论、语法、集合、免疫、色彩、逻辑与口味上填补缺口。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a puzzle piece whose edge fits exactly, leaving no gap.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块边线严丝合缝的拼图，不留缺口。

branches.en: THE FILLING PIECE: the thing supplied and the act of supplying it.
branches.cn: 填充的那块：被补上的东西与补上的动作。

branches.en: THE FULL COUNT: a set or crew brought to its required number.
branches.cn: 全额：组合或船员达到所需人数。

branches.en: THE CLAUSE AND THE PROPOSITION: what completes a sentence and what the first claim leaves outside itself.
branches.cn: 从句与命题：使句子完整的部分，以及首个陈述留在其外的东西。

branches.en: THE SET REMAINDER: everything not in a given set.
branches.cn: 集合的剩余：不在给定集合中的一切。

branches.en: THE BALANCED PAIR: proteins completing antibodies and colours completing each other.
branches.cn: 平衡的一对：完成抗体工作的蛋白与彼此补足的两种颜色。

intro.en: Complement is the Latin filling noun and verb; plere is the core and com- adds the togetherness.
intro.cn: complement 是拉丁语「填满」的名词与动词；plere 是核心，com- 加上「一起」。

latinIntro.en: Plere supplies the fill, complementum the thing that fills, and complere the act; compliment is a separate courtesy line.
latinIntro.cn: plere 提供「填」，complementum 提供填充之物，complere 提供动作；compliment 是另一条礼节线。

items.example: The prefix makes the filling complete rather than partial.
items.exampleCN: 前缀使填充完全，而不是部分。

items.example: The verb is the core of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是整个词族的核心。

items.structure: Latin verb from com- and plere
items.example: The compound adds the sense of reaching fullness.
items.exampleCN: 复合词加上「达到满」的意思。

items.example: The noun names the missing piece.
items.exampleCN: 名词命名缺失的那一块。

items.example: English keeps both the thing and the act.
items.exampleCN: 英语同时保留物与动作。

items.example: The adjective describes the relation between two parts.
items.exampleCN: 形容词描述两部分之间的关系。

items.example: The noun belongs to grammar and biology.
items.exampleCN: 名词用于语法与生物学。

items.example: The same filling verb gives the everyday word.
items.exampleCN: 同一「填满」动词给出日常词。

items.meaning: an addition to improve or extend
items.example: The word adds rather than completes.
items.exampleCN: 这个词是添加，而非补全。

items.example: The suffix turns the verb into the filling thing.
items.exampleCN: 后缀把动词变成填充之物。

definition_zh: 古生物学；古生物研究；以化石研究远古生命的学科实践
definition_en: the scientific study of ancient life through fossils, or the work and institutions devoted to it
core_image: 库房里，软刷清掉化石周围的砂岩，骨骼的轮廓一点点露出来
scene: 博物馆库房里，研究员用软刷清掉化石周围的砂岩，再量出骨骼的长度。 Paleontology often begins with a soft brush and a ruler rather than a hammer.
sceneCN: 这里 paleontology 指「古生物学这一学科及其研究实践」（第 1 个义项：以化石研究远古生命的学科）；句意为古生物学常常是从一把软刷和一把尺子开始，而不是从锤子开始。图中可辨识物件：软刷、砂岩、骨骼轮廓、卷尺、标本盒。

pos.zh: 古生物学；古生物研究（不可数）

derivatives.zh: 古生物学（偏生物学取向）

senses.title: The discipline itself
senses.definition: the branch of science that studies ancient organisms through their fossil remains
senses.definitionCN: 通过化石遗存研究远古生物的科学分支
senses.example: Paleontology sits between biology and geology and belongs fully to neither.
senses.exampleCN: 古生物学处在生物学与地质学之间，并不完全属于任何一方。
senses.why: the name is built from Greek 'old' plus 'beings' plus 'study', so it names a field defined by its object rather than its method.
senses.whyCN: 这个名称由希腊语「古老」「存在者」「研究」构成，因此它命名的是以对象而非方法界定的领域。

senses.title: The practice of studying fossils
senses.definition: the day-to-day work of excavating, preparing, measuring and interpreting fossil material
senses.definitionCN: 发掘、修整、测量与解释化石材料的日常工作
senses.example: Paleontology in the field means long hours of sieving and labelling.
senses.exampleCN: 野外的古生物学意味着长时间筛洗与贴标签。
senses.why: the same noun names the activity as well as the discipline, so a museum can say that paleontology is underway in its basement.
senses.whyCN: 同一名词既指学科也指活动，因此博物馆可以说地下室正在进行古生物研究。

senses.title: A university subject
senses.definition: a course of study or degree programme that trains students in fossil analysis
senses.definitionCN: 训练学生分析化石的课程或学位项目
senses.example: She took paleontology as her major after a summer of fieldwork.
senses.exampleCN: 一个夏天的野外工作之后，她把古生物学选为专业。
senses.why: institutional usage treats the field as a teachable curriculum with its own prerequisites.
senses.whyCN: 机构用法把这个领域当作有自身先修要求的可教课程。

senses.title: A museum department
senses.definition: the unit of a museum or institute that holds, prepares and researches fossil collections
senses.definitionCN: 博物馆或研究所中收藏、修整与研究化石的部门
senses.example: The paleontology department lent the skull for the exhibition.
senses.exampleCN: 古生物部门把这具头骨借给了展览。
senses.why: the word shifts from knowledge to the building and staff that produce it, a common institutional metonymy.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从知识转到生产知识的建筑与人员，是常见的机构转喻。

senses.title: Inference from fossil evidence
senses.definition: the method of reconstructing ancient life and environments from fossil evidence alone
senses.definitionCN: 仅凭化石证据重建远古生命与环境的方法
senses.example: Paleontology must infer behaviour from bones that cannot move.
senses.exampleCN: 古生物学只能从不能动的骨骼推断行为。
senses.why: the sense stresses the inference, because the objects of study no longer exist as living things.
senses.whyCN: 这一义强调推断，因为研究对象已不再作为活物存在。

senses.title: Fossils as dating tools
senses.definition: the use of fossil species to establish the relative age of rock layers
senses.definitionCN: 利用化石物种确定岩层相对年代的做法
senses.example: Paleontology supplies the index fossils that stratigraphers rely on.
senses.exampleCN: 古生物学提供地层学家所依赖的标志化石。
senses.why: biostratigraphy is where the field most directly serves geology, turning fossils into clocks.
senses.whyCN: 生物地层学是这个领域最直接服务地质学之处，把化石变成钟表。

senses.title: Public and amateur study
senses.definition: the study of fossils by interested non-specialists, in clubs, museums and online communities
senses.definitionCN: 有兴趣的非专业者在社团、博物馆与网络社群中研究化石
senses.example: Amateur paleontology has found some of the best specimens in the collection.
senses.exampleCN: 业余古生物研究为馆藏贡献了若干最好的标本。
senses.why: the noun does not require a degree, so collecting clubs legitimately practise paleontology at a small scale.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词并不要求学位，因此收藏社团在小规模上也在从事古生物学。

senses.title: A named subfield
senses.definition: one of the specialized branches, such as vertebrate or invertebrate paleontology
senses.definitionCN: 专门化分支之一，如脊椎动物或无脊椎动物古生物学
senses.example: Vertebrate paleontology grew around the first complete skeletons.
senses.exampleCN: 脊椎动物古生物学围绕最早的一批完整骨架发展起来。
senses.why: branches are named by adding the group studied, so paleontology functions as a head word in compounds.
senses.whyCN: 分支通过加上所研究的类群来命名，因此 paleontology 在复合词中充当中心词。

intro.en: Paleontology was coined in the early nineteenth century from Greek palaios 'old', onta 'beings' and -logia 'study'. The British spelling palaeontology keeps the digraph. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: paleontology 于十九世纪初由希腊 palaios「古老」、onta「存在者」与 -logia「研究」构成。英式拼写 palaeontology 保留二合元音。年代均为约数。

items.en: Palaios meant 'old, ancient', and it opens a large family of scientific words about the distant past.
items.cn: 一般认为 palaios 意为「古老的」，它开启了一大批关于远古的科学词。

items.en: Onta is the neuter plural of on 'being', so the middle element literally means 'existing things'.
items.cn: onta 是 on「存在者」的中性复数，因此中间成分字面意为「存在的事物」。

items.en: -logia 'the study of' comes from logos 'word, account, reason' and names disciplines from biology to geology.
items.cn: -logia「对……的研究」来自 logos「言说、道理」，用于命名从生物学到地质学的学科。

items.en: French zoologists of the early nineteenth century assembled the three elements to name the study of extinct organisms.
items.cn: 十九世纪初的法国动物学家把这三个成分组合起来，命名对已灭绝生物的研究。

items.en: British usage keeps palaeo-, American usage prefers paleo-, and both refer to the same field.
items.cn: 英式用法保留 palaeo-，美式用法多用 paleo-，两者指同一领域。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dating only): the Greek elements are certain, but the exact year and author of the coinage are disputed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：希腊成分确定，但造词的确切年份与作者尚有争议。

note.en: Group one separates paleontology from its spelling variants and derived names; group two separates it from neighbouring disciplines.
note.cn: 第一组把 paleontology 与拼写变体及派生名称分开；第二组区分它与相邻学科。

entries.definition: The same discipline written with the digraph ae, standard in British and Commonwealth usage.
entries.definitionCN: 同一学科，用二合元音 ae 拼写，通行于英国与英联邦。

entries.definition: The practitioner; the discipline and its worker differ only by the agent suffix.
entries.definitionCN: 从业者；学科与其从业者只差一个施事后缀。

entries.definition: Paleo- plus anthropology: the study of ancient humans specifically, a subfield rather than a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: paleo- 加 anthropology：专门研究远古人类，是分支而非同义词。

entries.definition: Paleo- plus geography: the mapping of ancient land and sea, which uses fossils but is not the study of life.
entries.definitionCN: paleo- 加 geography：重建古代陆海分布，会用到化石，但不研究生命本身。

entries.definition: The study of rocks, structures and earth history; paleontology borrows its methods but asks about organisms.
entries.definitionCN: 研究岩石、构造与地球历史；古生物学借其方法，但追问的是生物。

entries.definition: The study of past human societies through their material traces; it deals with people, not deep time.
entries.definitionCN: 通过物质遗存研究过去人类社会；对象是人，而非深时间。

entries.definition: The study of living organisms and their processes; paleontology applies biological questions to extinct forms.
entries.definitionCN: 研究活体生物及其过程；古生物学把生物学问题应用于已灭绝的形态。

entries.definition: The study of rock sequences and their order; it supplies the time frame in which fossils are placed.
entries.definitionCN: 研究岩层序列与次序；它为化石提供时间框架。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek palaios 'old' + onta 'beings' + -logia 'study': the study of ancient beings.
normal.cn: 希腊 palaios「古老」+ onta「存在者」+ -logia「研究」：对远古存在者的研究。

normal.en: The family runs paleontology, paleontologist, paleontological, paleobiology, paleoanthropology.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 paleontology、paleontologist、paleontological、paleobiology、paleoanthropology。

normal.en: Spelling: British palaeo-, American paleo-, same field.
normal.cn: 拼写：英式 palaeo-，美式 paleo-，同一领域。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: vertebrate paleontology, paleontology collection, paleontology department.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：脊椎动物古生物学、古生物藏品、古生物系。

normal.en: Keep it apart from archaeology, which studies people rather than extinct life.
normal.cn: 与 archaeology 分开，后者研究人，而非已灭绝的生命。

abstract.en: Picture a brush moving sand grain by grain off a rib.
abstract.cn: 想象刷子一粒一粒把沙从肋骨上拨开。

abstract.en: Picture a bone that can no longer move but still tells how it moved.
abstract.cn: 想象一块再也不能动的骨头，却仍能说明它曾如何运动。

abstract.en: Picture a library where every book is a stone page written by a dead animal.
abstract.cn: 想象一座图书馆，每本书都是一页由死去的动物写成的石头。

examples.en: Paleontology depends on comparative anatomy more than on chemistry.
examples.cn: 古生物学更依赖比较解剖学，而非化学。

examples.en: The paleontology collection holds over forty thousand specimens.
examples.cn: 该古生物藏品超过四万件标本。

examples.en: Field paleontology begins with recording where every fragment came from.
examples.cn: 野外古生物学从记录每一块碎片的出处开始。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「paleo（古老）+ onto（存在者）+ logy（学问）」——研究古老生命的学问 → 古生物学

root: 希腊 palaios「古老」+ onta「存在者」（on 的中性复数）+ -logia「研究」；十九世纪初法国动物学造词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the discipline to its daily work, its teaching, its museum home, its inference, its dating service, its amateur wing and its named branches.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从学科本身走到日常工作、教学、博物馆归属、推断方法、定年服务、业余一翼与命名的各分支。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a brush, a ruler and a label, applied to a bone that will never move again.
core.cn: 核心意象：软刷、尺子与标签，用在一块再也不会动的骨头上。

branches.en: DISCIPLINE AND WORK: the noun covers both the field and the labour inside it.
branches.cn: 学科与工作：这个名词兼指领域与其内部的劳作。

branches.en: INSTITUTIONS: a major and a museum department are the field made teachable and housed.
branches.cn: 机构：专业与博物馆部门，是学科变得可教、可存放的形态。

branches.en: METHOD AND SERVICE: inference about life, and dating for geology.
branches.cn: 方法与服务：对生命的推断，以及对地质学的定年。

branches.en: AMATEUR WING: the field does not require a degree to be practised.
branches.cn: 业余一翼：从事这一领域并不需要学位。

branches.en: NAMED BRANCHES: the head word builds subfields by adding the group studied.
branches.cn: 命名的分支：中心词通过加上所研究的类群构成分支。

intro.en: Paleontology is a three-part Greek compound, and each element still works in dozens of scientific words.
intro.cn: paleontology 是三段式希腊复合词，每个成分仍在数十个科学词中运作。

latinIntro.en: Greek palaios 'old', onta 'beings' and -logia 'study' combine; the same -logia builds geology, biology and archaeology.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 palaios「古老」、onta「存在者」与 -logia「研究」组合；同一 -logia 还构成 geology、biology 与 archaeology。

items.example: The prefix marks distance in time.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出时间上的遥远。

items.example: The element names what is studied, not how.
items.exampleCN: 这个成分命名研究对象，而非方法。

items.example: Biology and geology share the same suffix.
items.exampleCN: 生物学与地质学共用同一后缀。
古生物学从化石贝壳开始。
古生物学家测绘了采坑。

items.meaning: of the study of ancient life
items.exampleCN: 古生物学证据是间接的。

items.example: Paleobiology asks how the animal lived.
items.exampleCN: 古生物学追问这动物如何生活。
古人类学追踪早期人科。
古地理学重建古海岸线。

definition_zh: 纺织艺术；纤维艺术
definition_en: art made from fibre, thread, cloth or other soft materials
core_image: 画廊里一幅由粗麻、棉线与羊毛缝成的立体作品，从墙面微微凸出
scene: 画廊把旧床单、羊毛与棉线缝成一幅悬挂作品。 The gallery sewed old sheets, wool and cotton thread into a hanging work of textile art.
sceneCN: 这里指「以纤维与织物为材料的艺术门类」（第 1 个义项：纺织作为艺术创作）；句意为画廊把旧床单、羊毛与棉线缝成一件悬挂的纺织艺术作品。可辨识物件：旧床单、羊毛团、棉线、针、悬挂作品。

pos.zh: 纺织艺术（作为艺术门类）
纺织艺术作品（单件或集合）

forms.label: 复数形式（指多个门类或作品）

derivatives.zh: 纺织艺术家（由本短语前半与表示「艺术家」的词复合，语义收窄为职业身份）
纺织艺术作品（由本短语前半与表示「作品」的词复合，指具体成品）
纺织艺术门类（由本短语前半与表示「门类」的复数形式复合，指类别下的多种形式）
以纺织艺术为基础的（由本短语与表示「以……为基础」的词复合，语义偏移为属性描述）

senses.title: Art made from fibre
senses.titleCN: 以纤维为材料的艺术门类
senses.definition: art whose main material is fibre, thread, yarn or cloth rather than paint or stone
senses.definitionCN: 以纤维、线、纱或布为主要材料、而非颜料或石头的艺术
senses.example: The gallery sewed old sheets and wool into textile art.
senses.exampleCN: 画廊把旧床单与羊毛缝成纺织艺术。
senses.why: The phrase names a field by its material. Unlike painting, the work is built from soft, flexible strands that can be sewn, knotted or wrapped.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语按材料命名一个领域。与绘画不同，作品由柔软可弯的线构成，可以缝、结或缠绕。

senses.title: Traditional domestic crafts
senses.definition: the older craft traditions of weaving, embroidery, quilting and lace that the art grew from
senses.definitionCN: 纺织艺术所源自的织造、刺绣、绗缝与蕾丝等古老手工传统
senses.example: Textile art began in household weaving and embroidery.
senses.exampleCN: 纺织艺术起源于家庭织造与刺绣。
senses.why: Every culture made cloth at home. When those skills moved from use to display, they became an art with a lineage.
senses.whyCN: 每种文化都在家里制布。当这些技能从实用转向展示，它们就成了有谱系的技艺门类。

senses.title: Gallery fibre art
senses.definition: the movement from the 1960s that brought woven and fibre works into art galleries
senses.definitionCN: 二十世纪六十年代起把编织与纤维作品带进美术馆的运动
senses.example: Textile art entered the gallery with large hanging pieces.
senses.exampleCN: 纺织艺术以大型悬挂作品进入画廊。
senses.why: Artists pushed craft materials into the fine-art space, and critics needed a term that claimed gallery status without hiding the fibre.
senses.whyCN: 艺术家把手工材料推进纯艺术空间，评论界需要一个既主张画廊地位、又不掩盖纤维材料的说法。

senses.title: Sculptural textile forms
senses.definition: three-dimensional textile work built by stuffing, wrapping, hanging or stiffening cloth
senses.definitionCN: 通过填充、缠绕、悬挂或硬化布料做成的三维纺织作品
senses.example: Her textile art hangs from the ceiling in loops.
senses.exampleCN: 她的纺织艺术以环状从天花板垂下。
senses.why: Cloth can hold a shape once it is stuffed or sized, so the material leaves the wall and becomes sculpture.
senses.whyCN: 布料一旦被填充或上浆就能保持形状，于是材料离开墙面，成为雕塑。

senses.title: Wearable textile art
senses.definition: garments or body pieces made as artworks rather than as ordinary clothing
senses.definitionCN: 作为艺术品而非日常服装制作的衣物或身体作品
senses.example: The show presented textile art worn by the models.
senses.exampleCN: 这场秀让模特穿上了纺织艺术作品。
senses.why: Clothing is the body's nearest textile, so the art can move onto the body and be worn rather than viewed.
senses.whyCN: 衣物是身体最近的织物，因此这门艺术可以移到身体上，被穿着而非被观看。

senses.title: Narrative and ceremonial cloth
senses.definition: traditional cloth made to record events, mark rank or serve in ceremony
senses.definitionCN: 为记录事件、标示身份或用于礼仪而制作的传统织物
senses.example: Textile art in the village records weddings and harvests.
senses.exampleCN: 村里的纺织艺术记录婚礼与收成。
senses.why: Before writing was common, patterned cloth carried genealogy, status and ritual, so the art served memory as well as beauty.
senses.whyCN: 在书写普及之前，带图案的布承载世系、身份与礼仪，因此这门艺术既服务美，也服务记忆。

senses.title: Installation and public space
senses.titleCN: 装置与公共空间中的纺织艺术
senses.definition: large textile works installed in public buildings, streets or landscapes
senses.definitionCN: 安装在公共建筑、街道或景观中的大型纺织作品
senses.example: Textile art wrapped the bridge for one summer.
senses.exampleCN: 纺织艺术在一个夏天里包裹了那座桥。
senses.why: Because cloth is light and can be tied, wrapped and hung, it suits temporary works that change a whole place rather than one wall.
senses.whyCN: 布料轻，可系、可裹、可挂，因此适合改变整个场所而非一面墙的临时作品。

senses.title: A taught studio discipline
senses.definition: textile art as a course of study with techniques, materials and critique
senses.definitionCN: 作为一门有技法、材料与评论体系的学科来教授
senses.example: The school offers textile art as a three-year course.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校开设三年制的纺织艺术课程。
senses.why: Once the field had exhibitions and history, it needed teaching. The phrase then names a curriculum as well as a body of work.
senses.whyCN: 这门领域有了展览与历史之后就需要教学。这个短语于是既指一批作品，也指一套课程。

intro.en: Textile art joins the Latin word for woven cloth with the Latin word for skill. Both halves are old borrowings, and the compound is modern. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: textile art 把拉丁语中表示「织成的布」的词与表示「技艺」的词并在一起。两半都是古老借词，组合却是现代的。年代均为约数。

items.en: Latin texere 'to weave' gave textilis 'woven'. The verb treats cloth and language as the same act of binding strands.
items.cn: 拉丁 texere「编织」给出 textilis「织成的」。这个动词把布料与语言都看作同一种「把线束在一起」的动作。

items.en: Latin ars (genitive artis) meant 'skill, craft'. Its deeper origin is source uncertain, and the root sometimes proposed for it is a reconstructed form.
items.cn: 拉丁 ars（属格 artis）意为「技艺、手艺」。其更深来源属「来源不确定」，常为其提出的词根只是重构形式。

items.en: Old French carried both art and textile into English, where art long meant learned skill before it narrowed to the fine arts.
items.cn: 古法语把 art 与 textile 都带进英语；art 长期指习得的技艺，后来才收窄到美术。

items.en: The nineteenth-century craft revival began to treat weaving and embroidery as art rather than mere household work.
items.cn: 十九世纪的手工艺复兴开始把织造与刺绣当作艺术，而不只是家务劳动。

items.en: In the second half of the twentieth century textile art became a gallery and academic term, often overlapping with fibre art.
items.cn: 二十世纪下半叶，textile art 成为画廊与学术用语，常与纤维艺术一词重叠。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Latin origins of both texere and ars are unresolved, so older forms offered for them are reconstructed forms rather than recorded words.
items.cn: 来源不确定：texere 与 ars 在拉丁语之前的来源都没有定论，因此为它们提出的更早形式属于重构形式，而非有记录的真实词形。

note.en: Group one holds phrases built from the same words that name narrower things; group two holds names for neighbouring art practices.
note.cn: 第一组是由同样几个词构成、却指更窄事物的短语；第二组是相邻艺术实践的名称。

entries.definition: cloth itself; the longer phrase names the art made from it.
entries.definitionCN: 布料本身；较长的短语指用它创作的艺术。

entries.definition: the design of patterns and structures for manufactured cloth; it serves industry rather than the gallery.
entries.definitionCN: 为工业生产的布料设计图案与结构；它服务工业，而非画廊。

entries.definition: the plural form names the branches or the school subject as a whole; it is not a different art form.
entries.definitionCN: 复数形式指各个分支或整门学科；它不是另一种艺术形式。

entries.definition: a person who makes work in this medium; the compound names the maker.
entries.definitionCN: 用这种媒介创作的人；这个复合词指创作者。

entries.definition: a term coined in the mid twentieth century for art made from fibre; it overlaps with textile art but stresses the material rather than the cloth.
entries.definitionCN: 二十世纪中叶为纤维艺术创造的说法；与纺织艺术重叠，但强调材料而非布。

entries.definition: sculpture made from soft materials such as cloth, foam or vinyl; it is one branch of textile art rather than its name.
entries.definitionCN: 用布、海绵或乙烯基等软材料做的雕塑；它是纺织艺术的一支，而非其名称。

entries.definition: art made in craft media such as clay, glass, wood or fibre; it is wider than textile art.
entries.definitionCN: 用陶、玻璃、木或纤维等手工材料创作的艺术；比纺织艺术更宽泛。

entries.definition: art designed to be worn on the body; it can be made of textile but is defined by use, not material.
entries.definitionCN: 设计来穿在身体上的艺术；可以用纺织材料制作，但按用途而非材料定义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The phrase is material plus skill: the art of the woven thing.
normal.cn: 这个短语是材料加技艺：织成之物的艺术。

normal.en: Textile goes back to the verb 'to weave', and art goes back to 'skill', so the two halves name exactly what the field is.
normal.cn: textile 上溯到「编织」动词，art 上溯到「技艺」，两半正好说出了这个领域的本质。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark its settings: contemporary, traditional, exhibition, gallery.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出它的场合：当代的、传统的、展览、画廊。

normal.en: A textile artist is the maker; textile art is the field.
normal.cn: textile artist 指创作者；textile art 指领域。

normal.en: The plural textile arts covers the branches taught under one heading.
normal.cn: 复数形式涵盖同一名目下所教的各个分支。

abstract.en: Picture a painting that can be folded, worn and walked through.
abstract.cn: 想象一幅可以折叠、穿在身上、也能走进去的画。

abstract.en: Picture a family quilt that is also a gallery piece.
abstract.cn: 想象一床家用被子同时是画廊作品。

abstract.en: Picture an art whose material was once everyone's daily labour.
abstract.cn: 想象一门艺术，它的材料曾是每个人的日常劳动。

examples.en: The biennial gives textile art a whole floor.
examples.cn: 这届双年展给了纺织艺术整整一层。

examples.en: Her textile art uses hospital sheets and red thread.
examples.cn: 她的纺织艺术使用医院床单与红线。

examples.en: Textile art students learn dyeing before construction.
examples.cn: 纺织艺术学生先学染色，再学构造。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「纺织艺术」：把布料与线当作颜料和画笔 → 用纤维创作的艺术

root: 由 textile 与 art 组合：textile 经法语上溯至拉丁 textilis「织成的」，源自 texere「编织」；art 经古法语上溯至拉丁 ars「技艺」。两者的更早来源均不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one material into art: fibre itself, the domestic crafts behind it, the gallery, sculpture, the worn body, ceremonial cloth, public installation and finally the classroom.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让同一种材料走进艺术：纤维本身、其后的家庭手艺、画廊、雕塑、被穿上的身体、礼仪织物、公共装置，最后是教室。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: soft strands stitched and hung until they hold a shape in space.
core.cn: 核心意象：柔软的线被缝起、挂起，直到在空间中撑出一个形状。

branches.en: THE FIELD: the phrase first claims fibre as an art material.
branches.cn: 领域：这个短语首先把纤维确立为艺术材料。

branches.en: THE OLD CRAFTS: domestic weaving and ceremonial cloth are the tradition the art inherits.
branches.cn: 古老手艺：家庭织造与礼仪织物是这门艺术继承的传统。

branches.en: THE INSTITUTION: the gallery and the classroom turn the craft into a recognised discipline.
branches.cn: 机构：画廊与教室把这门手艺变成被承认的学科。

branches.en: IN SPACE: sculpture and installation take cloth off the wall and into three dimensions.
branches.cn: 在空间中：雕塑与装置把布离开墙面，带进三维空间。

branches.en: ON THE BODY: wearable work makes the viewer into the support.
branches.cn: 在身体上：可穿戴作品让观者本人成为承托物。

intro.en: The phrase joins a weaving root to a root for skill, and both sides bring large families of English words.
intro.cn: 这个短语把「编织」词根接到「技艺」词根上，两边都为英语带来庞大的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin texere gives textile, texture, text and context; Latin ars gives art, artist, artistic and artisan.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 texere 给出 textile、texture、text 与 context；拉丁 ars 给出 art、artist、artistic 与 artisan。

items.structure: texere, texui, textum (Latin verb, third conjugation)
items.example: The verb binds strands into a surface.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把线束成一片表面。

items.example: Textilis is the source of textile.
items.exampleCN: textilis 是 textile 的来源。

items.example: Textile is the material of the art.
items.exampleCN: 纺织材料是这门艺术的媒介。
在纺织艺术中，表面手感很重要。
ars 指习得的技艺。

items.example: Textile art claims a place among the arts.
items.exampleCN: 纺织艺术在艺术之列争取一席之地。
这位艺术家用羊毛创作。
这件作品有艺术抱负。

items.meaning: art made from cloth and fibre
items.meaningCN: 用织物与纤维创作的艺术
items.example: Textile art fills the upper gallery.
items.exampleCN: 纺织艺术占满上层画廊。

items.meaning: a person who makes textile art
items.example: The textile artist dyes her own thread.
items.exampleCN: 这位纺织艺术家自己染线。

definition_zh: 外骨骼；节肢动物体表起支撑与保护作用的硬壳；几丁质表皮本身；甲壳类与贝类的钙质外壳；蜕下的旧壳；化石中的外骨骼；可穿戴的机械外骨骼；建筑或器械的外部承力骨架（比喻）
definition_en: a hard outer covering that supports and protects the body of an arthropod or other invertebrate, lying outside the soft tissues
core_image: 潮间带的石头上，一只蟹抬起青灰色的硬壳，关节间露出薄薄的软膜
scene: 潮间带的石头上，一只蟹抬起硬壳，关节间露出薄薄的软膜。 On the tidal rock, a crab lifts its hard exoskeleton on thin flexible joints.
sceneCN: 这里 exoskeleton 指「节肢动物体表起支撑与保护作用的硬壳」（第 1 个义项：外骨骼）；句意为潮间带石头上的一只蟹抬起硬壳，关节处只留薄膜相连。可辨识物件：青灰硬壳、关节薄膜、石面、蟹步足。

pos.zh: 外骨骼；甲壳；外部承力骨架

senses.title: A hard outer support
senses.titleCN: 起支撑与保护作用的外部硬壳
senses.definition: a rigid outer covering that gives the body shape and protection while the muscles attach inside it
senses.definitionCN: 坚硬的包被，为身体定形并提供保护，肌肉在其内侧附着
senses.example: On the tidal rock, a crab lifts its hard exoskeleton on thin flexible joints.
senses.exampleCN: 潮间带的石头上，一只蟹抬起硬壳，关节处只留薄膜相连。
senses.why: The word says where the support lies: outside the soft body, opposite to our own internal frame.
senses.whyCN: 这个词说明了支撑的位置：在柔软身体之外，与我们的内置支架相反。

senses.title: The chitinous cuticle
senses.definition: the layered cuticle of chitin and protein that forms the outer body wall of insects and crustaceans
senses.definitionCN: 由几丁质与蛋白质分层构成、成为昆虫与甲壳类体壁的外层
senses.example: The insect's exoskeleton is a cuticle that must be shed to allow growth.
senses.exampleCN: 昆虫的外骨骼是一层必须蜕去才能生长的表皮。
senses.why: This technical sense identifies the material, not just the function, and it explains why the animal must moult.
senses.whyCN: 这一技术义指出材料而非仅指功能，也解释了动物为何必须蜕皮。

senses.title: A calcareous shell
senses.titleCN: 钙质外壳（甲壳类与贝类）
senses.definition: a shell hardened with calcium carbonate, as in crabs, barnacles or molluscs
senses.definitionCN: 以碳酸钙硬化的外壳，如蟹、藤壶或软体动物
senses.example: Barnacles build a calcareous exoskeleton around themselves.
senses.exampleCN: 藤壶在自己周围造出钙质外壳。
senses.why: Shells are one kind of exoskeleton, but not every shell is an arthropod cuticle, so the words overlap only partly.
senses.whyCN: 壳是外骨骼的一种，但并非所有壳都是节肢动物表皮，两词只是部分重叠。

senses.title: A cast-off outer casing
senses.definition: the old covering left behind after moulting, often found intact and empty
senses.definitionCN: 蜕皮后留下的旧包被，常完整而空心地被发现
senses.example: A dry exoskeleton clung to the reed at the pond edge.
senses.exampleCN: 一具干枯的旧壳粘在池边的芦苇上。
senses.why: This sense focuses on the object rather than the living animal, which matters when ecologists count moults.
senses.whyCN: 这一义聚焦物件而非活体，生态学家清点蜕壳时正需要这个意思。

senses.title: Fossil outer coverings
senses.definition: the preserved outer skeleton of extinct arthropods, often the only part that survives
senses.definitionCN: 已灭绝节肢动物被保存下来的外壳，常是唯一留存的部分
senses.example: Trilobite exoskeletons are common in Cambrian shale.
senses.exampleCN: 三叶虫的外骨骼在寒武纪页岩中很常见。
senses.why: Because the hard part is outside, fossil record is biased toward exoskeletons, a point palaeontology always notes.
senses.whyCN: 由于坚硬部分在体外，化石记录偏向保存外骨骼，古生物学总会强调这一点。

senses.title: A wearable mechanical frame
senses.definition: a powered frame worn outside the body to support or amplify movement
senses.definitionCN: 穿在身体外部、用于支撑或放大动作的动力框架
senses.example: The worker wore an exoskeleton that carried the load to his hips.
senses.exampleCN: 工人穿了一副把重量传到髋部的机械外骨骼。
senses.why: Engineering copied the biological word because the frame, like a shell, carries forces outside the soft body.
senses.whyCN: 工程学仿用了这个生物词，因为框架如外壳一样，在柔软身体之外承担力量。

senses.title: An external load-bearing frame
senses.titleCN: 建筑或器械的外部承力骨架
senses.definition: a structure that carries loads on its outside, as in some towers or vehicle chassis
senses.definitionCN: 在外侧承担荷载的结构，如某些塔架或车辆底盘
senses.example: The tower's exoskeleton of steel tubes takes the wind load.
senses.exampleCN: 这座塔的钢管外骨架承受风荷载。
senses.why: The metaphor moves from animals to structures but keeps the key idea: strength outside, softness inside.
senses.whyCN: 比喻从动物移到结构，却保留了要点：外强内柔。

senses.title: A protective outward manner
senses.definition: a hard outward manner or system that shields something softer inside
senses.definitionCN: 一层坚硬的对外姿态或制度，保护其中较柔软的部分
senses.example: His exoskeleton of rules hid a very anxious man.
senses.exampleCN: 他那层规章的外壳藏着一个极焦虑的人。
senses.why: The metaphor is emotional rather than mechanical: the shell protects but also isolates.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻是情感性的而非机械性的：外壳既保护也隔离。

intro.en: Exoskeleton joins Greek exo- 'outside' to skeleton, from Greek skeletos 'dried up, a mummy'. Nineteenth-century comparative anatomy coined the term to contrast with endoskeleton.
intro.cn: exoskeleton 把希腊 exo-「外面」与 skeleton 组合，后者出自希腊 skeletos「干枯的、木乃伊」。19 世纪比较解剖学造出这个词，与 endoskeleton 对照。

items.en: Exo- meant 'outside, outward' and remains productive in English, as in exoskeleton, exothermic and exoplanet.
items.cn: exo- 意为「外面、向外」，在英语中仍能产词，如 exoskeleton、exothermic、exoplanet。

items.en: Skeleton came from Greek skeletos 'dried up', used of a mummy or a withered body, and only later meant the bony frame.
items.cn: skeleton 出自希腊 skeletos「干枯的」，本用于木乃伊或干瘪的尸体，后来才指骨性支架。

items.en: Nineteenth-century anatomists needed paired terms for internal and external supports, and exoskeleton was formed against the older endoskeleton.
items.cn: 19 世纪解剖学家需要一对表示内外支撑的术语，exoskeleton 是对较早的 endoskeleton 造出的对应词。

items.en: The word was applied to insects, crustaceans and molluscs, and to the cuticle as well as the shell.
items.cn: 这个词被用于昆虫、甲壳类与软体动物，既指外壳也指表皮。

items.en: In the twentieth and twenty-first centuries the term was borrowed for wearable frames and external building structures.
items.cn: 在 20 与 21 世纪，这个词被借用于可穿戴框架与建筑外骨架。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and coiner): the exact first use and whether one anatomist coined both terms together are not settled, so no single attribution should be treated as certain.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与首创者）：确切最早的用法、以及是否由同一位解剖学家造出这对术语，均无定论，不应把单一归属当作确定。

note.en: Group one sets exoskeleton against the internal frame and its own derivatives; group two lists the outer coverings that overlap with it.
note.cn: 第一组把 exoskeleton 与内骨骼及自身派生词对照；第二组列出与它语义重叠的外层包被。

entries.definition: An endoskeleton lies inside the soft tissue, as in vertebrates, so the two words name opposite arrangements.
entries.definitionCN: endoskeleton 位于软组织之内，如脊椎动物，两词指相反的布局。

entries.definition: Skeleton is the general word and can mean either arrangement, or a framework of any kind.
entries.definitionCN: skeleton 是通称，可指任一种布局，也可指任何骨架。

entries.definition: Exoskeletal describes what belongs to an outer skeleton and cannot replace the noun.
entries.definitionCN: exoskeletal 描述属外骨骼之物，不能替代名词。

entries.definition: The adverb is rare and mainly appears in technical description, not in general prose.
entries.definitionCN: 这个副词罕见，主要用于技术描述，不用于一般行文。

entries.definition: A shell is a hard outer covering, often calcareous; it may or may not be a true exoskeleton.
entries.definitionCN: shell 是坚硬外层，常为钙质；它可能是也可能不是真正的外骨骼。

entries.definition: A carapace is the shield covering the back of a crab or similar animal, part of its exoskeleton.
entries.definitionCN: carapace 指蟹类背部的甲盾，是外骨骼的一部分。

entries.definition: A cuticle is the outermost layer of an animal or plant; in arthropods it is the exoskeleton itself.
entries.definitionCN: cuticle 指动物或植物的最外层；在节肢动物身上它就是外骨骼。

entries.definition: Armour is the general word for protective covering, used of tanks and knights as well as animals.
entries.definitionCN: armour 是防护包被的通称，可用于坦克、骑士，也可用于动物。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Exo- 'outside' plus skeleton says exactly where the support sits.
normal.cn: exo-「外面」加 skeleton 直接说明支撑的位置。

normal.en: The family runs exoskeleton, exoskeletons, exoskeletal and exoskeletally.
normal.cn: 词族包括 exoskeleton、exoskeletons、exoskeletal 与 exoskeletally。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: shed the exoskeleton, robotic exoskeleton, calcareous exoskeleton.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：蜕去外骨骼、机械外骨骼、钙质外壳。

normal.en: The pair endoskeleton and exoskeleton differ only in the first prefix, endo- versus exo-.
normal.cn: 内骨骼与外骨骼这一对只差前缀：endo- 与 exo-。

normal.en: Arthropods must moult because their support cannot grow with them.
normal.cn: 节肢动物必须蜕皮，因为它们的支撑结构不能随身体一同长大。

abstract.en: Picture a knight whose armour is grown, not worn.
abstract.cn: 想象一位骑士，盔甲是长出来的，不是穿上的。

abstract.en: Picture a building that wears its steel frame on the outside.
abstract.cn: 想象一座把钢架穿在外面的建筑。

abstract.en: Picture a person whose politeness is a shell with a soft animal inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人，礼貌是壳，里面藏着一只柔软的小动物。

examples.en: A crab must back out of its old exoskeleton before the new one hardens.
examples.cn: 蟹必须在新壳硬化之前从旧壳里退出来。

examples.en: Paleontologists rely on exoskeletons because soft parts rarely fossilise.
examples.cn: 古生物学家依赖外骨骼，因为软体部分极少形成化石。

examples.en: The warehouse adopted a robotic exoskeleton to help workers lift heavy crates.
examples.cn: 仓库采用机械外骨骼来帮助工人抬起重箱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「exo（外）+ skeleton（骨架）」——长在身体外面的骨架 → 外骨骼

root: 希腊 exo-「外面」+ skeleton（希腊 skeletos「干枯的」，原指木乃伊或干瘪尸体）。19 世纪比较解剖学造词，与 endoskeleton 成对。确切首见年代与首创者不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move outward from the idea of support outside the body: the arthropod shell, the chitin layer, calcareous shells, cast moults, fossils, wearable frames, building frames and a defensive manner.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从「支撑在身体之外」这一想法向外展开：节肢动物硬壳、几丁质层、钙质壳、蜕壳、化石、可穿戴框架、建筑骨架与防御性的姿态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hard shell carried on the outside, muscles pulling from within, joints left soft.
core.cn: 核心意象：一具穿在外面的硬壳，肌肉从内侧牵引，关节处保持柔软。

branches.en: THE ARRANGEMENT: support outside, soft tissue inside.
branches.cn: 布局：支撑在外，软组织在内。

branches.en: THE MATERIALS: chitin and calcium carbonate are two ways of hardening the outside.
branches.cn: 材料：几丁质与碳酸钙是硬化外层的两种方式。

branches.en: WHAT IS LEFT: cast shells and fossils are the hard part without the animal.
branches.cn: 留下之物：蜕壳与化石都是失去动物后的硬部。

branches.en: ENGINEERING: wearable frames and building frames copy the load path.
branches.cn: 工程：可穿戴框架与建筑骨架复制了这条受力路径。

branches.en: PROTECTIVE MANNER: a hard outward habit shields something soft.
branches.cn: 防御姿态：坚硬的外在习惯护住柔软之物。

intro.en: Exoskeleton is a Greek-derived compound; the prefix exo-, the base skeleton and the adjective suffix -al all remain productive in English.
intro.cn: exoskeleton 是希腊来源的复合词；前缀 exo-、词基 skeleton 与形容词后缀 -al 在英语中均仍能产词。

latinIntro.en: Greek exō 'outside' gives the prefix exo-, as in exoskeleton and exothermic; Greek skeletos 'dried up' gives skeleton and skeletal.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 exō「外面」给出前缀 exo-，如 exoskeleton、exothermic；希腊 skeletos「干枯的」给出 skeleton 与 skeletal。

items.example: The prefix places the structure outside the body.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把结构置于体外。

items.example: The skeleton carries the body's weight.
items.exampleCN: 骨架承担身体的重量。

items.example: The exoskeleton protects the soft body.
items.exampleCN: 外骨骼保护柔软的身体。
蜕下的外骨骼散落岸边。
外骨骼板像瓦片一样重叠。

items.meaning: by means of an outer skeleton
items.exampleCN: 这种动物靠外骨骼支撑。
这个反应是放热的。

items.meaning: a planet outside the solar system
items.example: An exoplanet passed before its star.
items.exampleCN: 一颗系外行星从它的恒星前经过。

items.example: The exoskeleton suit halved the lifting effort.
items.exampleCN: 外骨骼服把举重费力减半。

definition_zh: n. 饵；诱饵；诱人上钩之物　v. 装饵于；下饵诱捕；故意激怒、逗弄
definition_en: food or a lure used to attract fish or animals; something that tempts a person into a trap; to put bait on or in; to deliberately annoy or provoke
core_image: 钩尖上那一小块颤动的鱼肉，水下有东西正盯着它
scene: 老渔夫往钩上挂了一小块鱼肉。 The old fisherman put a strip of fish on the hook as bait.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：bait 指引鱼上钩的食物；句意是老渔夫把一小条鱼肉挂在钩上当饵。

collocations.zh: 诱饵调包（先用低价引人再换货的销售手法）

forms.label: 第三人称单数／名词复数

senses.title: Food that lures
senses.definition: food placed on a hook or in a trap to attract fish or animals
senses.definitionCN: 放在钩上或陷阱里用来引鱼、引兽的食物
senses.example: He dug worms for bait before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 天亮前他挖了些蚯蚓当饵。
senses.why: The Old Norse source meant to make an animal bite, so the noun names whatever produces that bite.
senses.whyCN: 古诺斯语词源意为「使动物咬」，因此这个名词指能引出那一咬的东西。

senses.title: A tempting offer
senses.definition: something attractive offered so that a person will do what someone else wants
senses.definitionCN: 为让人按他人意愿行事而抛出的诱人条件
senses.example: The free trial was bait for a yearly contract.
senses.exampleCN: 免费试用只是引人签年度合同的诱饵。
senses.why: The fishing picture transfers to people: the offer is the worm, and the contract is the hook.
senses.whyCN: 钓鱼的画面被移用到人身上：优惠是那条虫，合同才是钩。

senses.title: To put bait on
senses.definition: to place food on a hook or in a trap, or to set a trap with food
senses.definitionCN: 把食物挂在钩上或放进陷阱，或用食物布置陷阱
senses.example: She baited the line and cast it past the reeds.
senses.exampleCN: 她给钓线装好饵，把钩甩过芦苇丛。
senses.why: English turns the noun into a verb with no change of form, a very common shift in the language.
senses.whyCN: 英语不改词形就把名词转为动词，这在该语言中极为常见。

senses.title: To provoke on purpose
senses.definition: to deliberately annoy or attack someone, especially to make them lose control
senses.definitionCN: 故意招惹或攻击某人，尤指使其失去自控
senses.example: The lawyer tried to bait the witness into shouting.
senses.exampleCN: 律师试图激怒证人，让他喊起来。
senses.why: An older sport set dogs on a chained animal; the same verb now describes needling a person until they snap.
senses.whyCN: 旧时有一种放犬撕咬拴住动物的把戏；同一个动词如今指把人撩到失控。

intro.en: Bait is a causative of bite: the Old Norse source meant to make something bite. From that single idea come the worm, the tempting offer, and the deliberate provocation.
intro.cn: bait 是 bite「咬」的使役形式：古诺斯语词源意为「使某物咬」。由这一个念头，生出鱼虫、诱饵与故意挑怒三层意思。

items.en: The deep root bheid meant to split or bite into, the same source as bite.
items.cn: 深层词根 bheid 意为劈开或咬入，与 bite 同源。

items.en: Germanic baitjan was a causative of bitan, so it meant to make something bite.
items.cn: 日耳曼语 baitjan 是 bitan 的使役形式，意为「使……咬」。

items.en: Old Norse beita meant to hunt with dogs, to pasture, and to feed a hook.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 beita 指用犬追猎、放牧，也指给钩上食。

items.en: Middle English beyt names food set out to make a fish or animal bite.
items.cn: 中古英语 beyt 指为使鱼或兽咬钩而摆出的食物。

items.en: Writers extend the word to any lure that tempts a person into a trap.
items.cn: 文人把该词扩展为任何诱人入局的诱惑物。

items.en: A second verb sense appears, to torment a chained animal, and later to needle a person.
items.cn: 又生出第二个动词义：折磨被拴住的动物，后来指故意激怒他人。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the same-sound bate and three rhymes; the near-meaning group covers the wider vocabulary of luring, from a false bird to thrown fish scraps.
note.cn: 形近组放同音的 bate 与三个押韵词；近义组覆盖「引诱」这一更大的词汇场，从假鸟到撒入水中的碎鱼。

entries.definition: To hold back or reduce, as in bated breath.
entries.definitionCN: 抑制或减弱，如 bated breath「屏息」。

entries.definition: Money paid to free an accused person before trial.
entries.definitionCN: 保释金；保释。

entries.definition: To stay until something happens.
entries.definitionCN: 等待。

entries.definition: The way a person or animal walks.
entries.definitionCN: 步态。

entries.definition: Anything that attracts and draws someone in.
entries.definitionCN: 任何吸引并引人入内之物。

entries.definition: A false figure used to draw birds or attention.
entries.definitionCN: 用来引鸟或转移注意的假物。

entries.definition: Something offered to persuade.
entries.definitionCN: 为劝诱而给出的好处。

entries.definition: Chopped fish thrown in the water to attract fish.
entries.definitionCN: 撒入水中引鱼的碎鱼饵。

normalIntro.en: Bait hides inside bite: change one vowel and you get the thing that makes a fish bite.
normalIntro.cn: bait 就藏在 bite 里：换一个元音，就得到那个「让鱼咬」的东西。

normal.en: Bite is what the fish does; bait is what you offer.
normal.cn: bite 是鱼做的动作，bait 是你递出的东西。

normal.en: A worm on a hook is bait in its first sense.
normal.cn: 钩上的蚯蚓是第一义的 bait。

normal.en: A free gift with a hidden contract is bait in its second sense.
normal.cn: 附赠礼品背后藏着合同，那是第二义的 bait。

normal.en: To bait a hook is to load it; to bait a person is to load them too.
normal.cn: bait a hook 是给钩装料，bait a person 是给人「装料」点火。

normal.en: Take the bait means swallow the hook along with the worm.
normal.cn: take the bait 就是连钩带虫一起吞下。

abstract.en: A small kindness with a sharp curve inside.
abstract.cn: 一点小小的善意，里面藏着一道尖锐的弯。

abstract.en: The visible part of an invisible arrangement.
abstract.cn: 一桩看不见的安排里，唯一看得见的那部分。

abstract.en: Anger offered as food until someone bites.
abstract.cn: 把怒气当食物递出去，直到有人咬下。

examples.en: The trout ignored the bait and drifted away.
examples.cn: 那条鳟鱼没理鱼饵，慢慢游开了。

examples.en: He baited the trap with a piece of cheese.
examples.cn: 他用一块奶酪给陷阱下了饵。

examples.en: Reporters baited her for hours, but she stayed calm.
examples.cn: 记者们撩了她几个小时，她始终平静。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「贝特」——把宝贝特意摆出来给你看，其实是 bait 诱饵。再记字形：bait 与 bite 只差一个元音，「让它咬」的东西就是饵。

root: 出自原始日耳曼语使役形式 baitjan「使咬」，与 bite 同源；古诺斯语 beita 兼有追猎、放牧、给钩上食三义，约 1300 年进入中古英语作 beyt。1590 年代生出「诱人入局」的比喻义，17 世纪又生出「故意激怒」的动词义。

sensesIntro.en: All four senses share one move: put something tempting in front of a creature and wait for it to bite.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项共用同一个动作：把一个诱人的东西摆到某个生物面前，然后等它咬下来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a strip of fish trembling on a hook while something watches from below
core.cn: 核心意象：钩尖上一小条颤动的鱼肉，水下有东西正盯着

branches.en: A tin of worms in the mud.
branches.cn: 泥地里一罐蚯蚓。

branches.en: A free month with a year attached.
branches.cn: 免费一个月，后面拴着一整年。

branches.en: A thumb pressing food onto the barb.
branches.cn: 拇指把食料按上倒刺。

branches.en: A question aimed at a sore spot.
branches.cn: 专往痛处戳的一句提问。

branches.en: The hook nobody is meant to see.

intro.en: Bait has no prefix of its own; it is a bare Germanic root. The endings below build its verb forms and the wider vocabulary of tempting.
